fixes.detail: Launch setup from the Windows Installation Assistant or from a mounted ISO and pick 'Keep personal files and apps'. If the rollback happens again, open `C:\$WINDOWS.~BT\Sources\Panther\setupact.log` and look for the driver or device that caused the failure.

prevention: Before a feature upgrade, confirm your hardware is on the PC maker's compatibility list (or run PC Health Check)
Update drivers and firmware before the upgrade instead of afterward
Uninstall older security suites before moving to a new Windows version
Create a full backup image ahead of every feature upgrade

title: Windows upgrade error 0xC1900208 (blocked by a compatibility check)
summary: Setup won't even begin the upgrade and reports 0xC1900208. Its compatibility check spotted an app or driver that can't run on the new version, and Windows holds the upgrade back until that item is updated or removed.
meaning: With 0xC1900208, the compatibility scan (or a check performed while setup runs) identified software or hardware that won't work on the target version of Windows. Common culprits are older antivirus, VPN and disk-utility programs, along with legacy drivers. This is an intentional safeguard, so setup stops cleanly and changes nothing on the PC. The item responsible is named either in the on-screen message or in the upgrade logs.
commonCauses: An app that setup flags as incompatible, very often antivirus or VPN software
Older drivers that have no Windows 10/11-compatible release
Virtualization or disk-encryption tools that need a newer version
A stale compatibility block left behind by an earlier upgrade attempt

fixes.title: Remove the app that setup flagged
fixes.detail: Find the name of the blocking item in the upgrade message or in the files under `C:\$WINDOWS.~BT\Sources\Panther\compatreport`. Uninstall it from Settings > Apps > Installed apps, then start the upgrade again.

fixes.title: Update the flagged program rather than uninstalling it
fixes.detail: Get the version of the app that the vendor supports on Windows 10/11 and install it. For security software in particular, this is usually the better route because it keeps the PC protected.

fixes.title: Update any driver named in the block
fixes.detail: When the block points at a driver, download and install the manufacturer's current release before trying again. Legacy drivers that are no longer supported trigger this block often.

fixes.title: Run the upgrade again once the block is gone
fixes.detail: Restart the PC, then launch the Installation Assistant or setup once more and make sure the compatibility check comes back clean. When it passes, setup moves on to the installation itself.

prevention: Run PC Health Check or the setup compatibility scan ahead of any major upgrade
Swap out software that its vendor no longer maintains before you upgrade
Keep security software on a version certified for the Windows release you run
Make a backup before feature upgrades, even when setup reports no blocks

title: Microsoft Store error 0x80D03805 (app download failed)
summary: An app download or update in the Microsoft Store stops with 0x80D03805. The usual reasons are a damaged Store cache, a network transfer that got cut off, or a system clock that is set wrong.
meaning: 0x80D03805 comes from the Store's delivery pipeline and means the app, its update or its license never finished downloading. Several things feed that pipeline: the Store's local download cache (which wsreset clears), a stable network connection, the state of the account you're signed in with, and the system clock. When a transfer is interrupted, leftover cached data can cause every retry to fail the same way.
commonCauses: A damaged Microsoft Store download cache
A network connection that dropped or was unstable mid-download
Wrong system date, time or region settings
Problems with the Store sign-in or the account itself
A VPN, proxy or firewall getting in the way
Too little free disk space to hold the app being downloaded

fixes.title: Clear the Store cache using wsreset
fixes.detail: Press Win+R, type `wsreset.exe` and press Enter. A blank window appears; once it closes and the Store opens by itself, try the download again. This is the go-to first step for Store download failures.

fixes.title: Confirm date, time and region
fixes.detail: In Settings > Time & language, turn on 'Set time automatically' and click Sync now, then make sure the region is correct. The Store checks downloads against both.

fixes.title: Sign out of the Store and sign in again
fixes.detail: Open the profile menu in the Store app and sign out. Close and reopen the Store, then sign back in so your account and license tokens are refreshed.

fixes.title: Use the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Store Apps, run it, accept any repairs it suggests, and retry the download.

fixes.title: Rule out the network, VPN and proxy
fixes.detail: Switch off any VPN, check Settings > Network & internet > Proxy and disable a proxy if one is set, and if you can, try a different network or a phone hotspot before retrying.

fixes.title: Re-register the Microsoft Store
fixes.detail: Open PowerShell as administrator and run `Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers Microsoft.WindowsStore | Foreach {Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register "$($_.InstallLocation)\AppXManifest.xml"}`. When it finishes, open the Store again.

prevention: Leave date and time on automatic
Run wsreset if downloads keep getting interrupted
Turn off VPNs while downloading large Store apps
Update the Store app itself from its Library page

title: Microsoft Store error 0x80131500 (Store service can't be reached)
summary: The Microsoft Store shows 0x80131500 when it can't get a response from Microsoft's Store services. Usually the system clock is wrong (which breaks secure connections), a proxy or VPN is interfering, the cache is damaged, or the service itself is down.
meaning: 0x80131500 is the Store's catch-all server error: it asked for content and didn't get a valid reply. All Store traffic travels over HTTPS, so a clock that is off breaks the secure handshake. Proxies and VPNs can reroute or block the connection, and a damaged local cache or an outage on Microsoft's end can produce the same result. A quick test from a different device or network tells you whether the problem is on your PC or with the service.
commonCauses: A wrong system date or time that breaks the secure connection
A proxy, VPN or firewall blocking access to Store services
A damaged Microsoft Store cache
An outage of the Microsoft Store service (wait it out and retry)
DNS trouble on your local network

fixes.title: Check the system date and time
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > Time & language, turn on 'Set time automatically' and click 'Sync now'. A clock that has drifted is the most frequent cause of this particular error.

fixes.title: Clear the Store cache using wsreset
fixes.detail: Press Win+R, run `wsreset.exe`, and wait until the Store reopens by itself. That wipes any damaged cached responses, so try again afterward.

fixes.title: Turn off VPN/proxy and try a different network
fixes.detail: Disconnect VPN software and clear any proxy settings under Settings > Network & internet > Proxy. If possible, test on another network so you can rule out filtering by your ISP.

fixes.title: Sign out of the Store and sign in again
fixes.detail: From the profile menu choose Sign out, close and reopen the Store app, then sign in again to get fresh account tokens.

fixes.title: Wait if Microsoft's service is down
fixes.detail: When a different device on a different network fails the same way, the Store service itself is probably having an outage. Give it 30-60 minutes and try again.

fixes.title: Re-register the Microsoft Store
fixes.detail: In PowerShell running as administrator, run `Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers Microsoft.WindowsStore | Foreach {Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register "$($_.InstallLocation)\AppXManifest.xml"}`, then launch the Store again.

prevention: Leave automatic time sync turned on
Where you can, let Store traffic go out directly instead of through a VPN or proxy
Run wsreset whenever the Store starts acting strangely
During suspected outages, check the service status before diving into deep troubleshooting

title: 0x80070422: ERROR_SERVICE_DISABLED (Windows Update or Store service turned off)
summary: You get 0x80070422 because a service the task relies on has its startup type set to Disabled, so Windows can't launch it. For updates and the Store, that is usually the Windows Update service, BITS or the Microsoft Store Install Service.
meaning: Behind 0x80070422 is the Win32 error ERROR_SERVICE_DISABLED (error 1058). The service is present on the system, but because its startup type is Disabled, Windows is not allowed to start it when it's needed. Windows Update and the Store depend on the Windows Update service (wuauserv), the Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) and the Microsoft Store Install Service (InstallService). These can be switched off by 'optimizer' utilities, group policy or malware, and the error then shows up the next time Windows looks for updates.
commonCauses: The Windows Update service (wuauserv) has been set to Disabled
The Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) is disabled
The Microsoft Store Install Service (InstallService) is disabled
A 'tweaking' or 'debloat' tool turned the services off
Malware or a group policy disabled the services

fixes.title: Turn the needed services back on
fixes.detail: Open `services.msc` and locate 'Windows Update', 'Background Intelligent Transfer Service' and 'Microsoft Store Install Service'. For each one, change Startup type to Manual (or Automatic), click Start, and then try the update again.

fixes.title: Let the Windows Update troubleshooter check things
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Update. The troubleshooter can spot disabled services and stuck configuration and fix them for you.

fixes.title: Check the PC for malware
fixes.detail: Run a full scan with Microsoft Defender. Certain threats shut down update and security services on purpose, and the services will keep getting disabled until the infection is cleaned up.

fixes.title: Repair system files using SFC and DISM
fixes.detail: From an elevated prompt, run `sfc /scannow`, follow it with `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`, and finish with another `sfc /scannow`. This restores service configuration that may have been damaged.

fixes.title: Review group policy (managed or advanced setups)
fixes.detail: On a work or school PC, open `gpedit.msc` and look at Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Update, or check with your IT team. A policy can force these services off.

prevention: Stay away from 'optimizer' tools that switch off Windows services
Keep Microsoft Defender turned on and current
After running any debloat script, run the Windows Update troubleshooter again
On company-managed PCs, agree on update policy with your IT department

title: ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND: Windows Update fails with 0x8007007e
summary: An update stops with 0x8007007e, 'The specified module could not be found'. The installer expected a component or DLL that is either missing or wouldn't load, which usually points to damaged system files or a damaged component store.
meaning: 0x8007007e is the HRESULT wrapper for Win32 error 126, ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND: the update process tried to load a module and couldn't find it. In the servicing context, that typically means a DLL or component the installer relies on has gone missing or become corrupted inside the component store or system files. Less often, security software prevented the module from loading.
commonCauses: Damage to the component store or to system files
A servicing component lost after an earlier update failed
Antivirus or other security software blocking modules from loading
Disk errors that have corrupted system DLLs
An app that was only partly uninstalled and took shared system components with it

fixes.title: Fix the component store with DISM, then run SFC
fixes.detail: Open an elevated prompt, run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`, and then run `sfc /scannow`. DISM puts back the missing or damaged modules the update is looking for.

fixes.title: Use the Windows Update troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Update, apply whatever fixes it proposes, and run the update again.

fixes.title: Clear the update cache (SoftwareDistribution)
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `net stop wuauserv` and `net stop bits`, rename `C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution` to `SoftwareDistribution.old`, then run `net start bits` and `net start wuauserv`. Check for updates once more.

fixes.title: Uninstall third-party antivirus for the update
fixes.detail: To rule out interference with module loading, remove the third-party security suite while the update installs and let Defender cover the PC. Put the suite back once you're done.
fixes.riskNote: Turn your protection back on as soon as the update has finished installing.

fixes.title: Install the update by hand from the Microsoft Update Catalog
fixes.detail: Look up the failing KB number on catalog.update.microsoft.com, download the standalone package, and run it. Standalone installers carry the modules they need.

prevention: Run DISM and SFC after any update that fails or gets interrupted
Replace drives that start reporting disk errors
Don't run aggressive 'debloat' scripts that strip out shared components
Keep 10-20 GB of free space on the system drive

title: E_FAIL: Unspecified error (0x80004005)
summary: When an operation fails and Windows has no more specific explanation, you see 'Unspecified error' (0x80004005). It turns up most often with Windows Update, when copying or extracting files, when opening Microsoft Store apps, and when starting virtual machines.
meaning: 0x80004005 is E_FAIL, the generic failure code used by COM and HRESULT-based components. Whatever component was doing the work ran into a problem it had no specific message for, so Windows falls back to the generic 'Unspecified error'. Since the code is generic, the real cause can be anything from damaged system files and permission issues to antivirus interference or a broken application.
commonCauses: System files or the Windows component store damaged by a failed update
Antivirus or other third-party security software blocking the action
Missing permissions, or ownership problems, on the files or folders involved
A broken app installation (Store apps, archive extractors, virtualization tools)
Low disk space or a failing drive cutting writes short

fixes.title: Restart, then try again
fixes.detail: Reboot and repeat the exact action that failed. A restart often clears temporary file locks and half-finished update states.

fixes.title: For update failures, run the Windows Update troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters and launch the Windows Update troubleshooter. Accept the fixes it suggests and then retry the update.

fixes.title: Repair system files with SFC
fixes.detail: Open Command Prompt or Terminal as Administrator and run `sfc /scannow`. Restart when the scan completes, even if it says nothing was found.

fixes.title: Repair the component store with DISM
fixes.detail: From the same elevated prompt, run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` and then `sfc /scannow` one more time. DISM rebuilds the store that SFC uses as its repair source.

fixes.title: Briefly disable third-party antivirus
fixes.detail: If you use a third-party security suite, switch it off for a moment and try the operation again, then turn it back on. Only add a trusted-folder exclusion once you've confirmed the suite was causing the failure.
fixes.riskNote: Don't visit untrusted websites while protection is off, and re-enable it right after the test.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the app involved
fixes.detail: When the error is tied to a specific app (a Store app, an extractor, virtualization software), go to Settings > Apps > Installed apps and choose Modify or Repair, or reinstall using a fresh installer from the vendor.

prevention: Keep Windows and drivers updated, and don't cut power while updates install
Run SFC and DISM after a crash or failed update to catch corruption early
Leave at least 15-20% of the system drive free
Use Windows Security (Defender), or keep third-party antivirus definitions up to date

title: ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (Access is denied)
summary: 'Access is denied' (system error 5) appears when a program, script or command tries something the current account doesn't have permission to do.
meaning: Windows returns Win32 error 5, ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, whenever its security model stops access to a file, folder, registry key, service or device. The most common triggers are running an administrator-only task without elevation, NTFS permissions or ownership that have been changed, and security software guarding a protected location.
commonCauses: Running a program or command without administrator rights (a non-elevated prompt)
Changed NTFS permissions or ownership, such as a file owned by another account or by TrustedInstaller
Controlled folder access (ransomware protection in Windows Security) blocking a write
Another process or user profile has the file open or locked
Third-party security software or a group policy restricting that location

fixes.title: Run the program as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program and pick Run as administrator, or open Windows Terminal or Command Prompt as Administrator and run the command again. A large share of 'Access is denied' errors come down to missing elevation.

fixes.title: Look at Controlled folder access in Windows Security
fixes.detail: Go to Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Ransomware protection. If Controlled folder access is turned on, check the list of blocked apps and allow the one that was refused.

fixes.title: Take ownership and correct the permissions
fixes.detail: In File Explorer, right-click the file or folder and open Properties > Security > Advanced. Change the Owner to your account, then give your account Full control. For folders, apply the change to child objects as well.
fixes.riskNote: Only change permissions on your own data. Editing ACLs on Windows system folders can weaken security or cause updates to fail.

fixes.title: Reset permissions using icacls (advanced)
fixes.detail: For a folder with broken ACLs, open an elevated prompt and run `icacls "C:\path\to\folder" /reset /t /c` to bring back inherited permissions. To give the Administrators group full control instead, use `icacls "C:\path" /grant "Administrators:F" /t`.
fixes.riskNote: Mass permission changes are difficult to reverse, so double-check the path before applying them to an entire folder tree.

fixes.title: Use Safe Mode when the file is locked
fixes.detail: If a running process is holding or protecting the file, restart into Safe Mode (Settings > System > Recovery > Advanced startup > Startup Settings) and do the copy or delete from there.

prevention: Launch admin tools with Run as administrator rather than turning UAC off
Leave permissions on C:\Windows, Program Files and other users' profiles alone
Keep a single admin account and do everyday work in a standard account
Adjust the Controlled folder access allow list instead of disabling the protection

title: ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (The system cannot find the file specified)
codes: The system cannot find the file specified
summary: Error 2, 'The system cannot find the file specified', shows up when a program, script or service goes looking for a file that isn't where it's supposed to be.
meaning: With ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, Windows could reach the folder in the path, but the file at the end of it wasn't there. It may have been deleted, moved or renamed, or it was never installed to begin with. You'll typically see it when opening apps through broken shortcuts or registry entries, when a service points to an executable that was removed, or after antivirus quarantined a file something needed.
commonCauses: The file was deleted, moved or renamed, possibly by a cleanup utility
A shortcut, scheduled task or registry Run key still references the old location
Antivirus quarantined or deleted the file by mistake
An unfinished uninstall left references to shared files that are now gone
A typo or the wrong drive letter in a command, script or config file

fixes.title: Confirm the file really exists at that path
fixes.detail: Browse to the exact folder in File Explorer, or run `dir "C:\path\to\file.ext"` in a prompt. Correct any typos or wrong drive letters first, since that alone fixes a lot of cases.

fixes.title: Restore the file from quarantine
fixes.detail: Check Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history (or the quarantine area of your antivirus). If the detection was a false positive, restore the file and add an exclusion for the trusted program's folder.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the app
fixes.detail: In Settings > Apps > Installed apps, choose Modify or Repair for the app, or run its original installer and select Repair. That puts missing program files back and fixes broken registration.

fixes.title: Remove broken shortcuts and startup items
fixes.detail: Fix or delete any shortcut that throws the error when opened. If the error appears at startup, check Task Manager > Startup apps and the `shell:startup` folder for entries pointing at files that no longer exist.

fixes.title: Run SFC when a Windows file is the one missing
fixes.detail: If the missing file belongs to Windows itself (for example, Event Viewer shows the error coming from a system component), run `sfc /scannow` from an elevated prompt. If problems remain, follow up with `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`.

prevention: Remove software through its uninstaller rather than deleting its folders
After any antivirus detection, check the quarantine instead of assuming it got it right
Leave System Restore enabled so you can get back moved or deleted files
Use full, verified paths in scripts and scheduled tasks

title: ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (The parameter is incorrect)
summary: Error 87, 'The parameter is incorrect', means a program or command handed Windows an argument it rejected as invalid. It's common with command-line tools such as DISM, robocopy and netsh, during System Restore, and when the component store is corrupted.
meaning: Windows returns ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER when a command or function call contains an argument that is badly formed, out of range, or not supported by the Windows build you're running. It points at the command or the software calling Windows, not at a missing file. A textbook case is DISM failing with error 87 on very old builds that don't recognize newer switches.
commonCauses: Wrong command syntax, or a switch the installed Windows build doesn't support
Damaged system files passing bad data to Windows APIs
Badly formed paths, such as trailing spaces, illegal characters, or mixing up UNC paths and drive letters
Third-party programs sending invalid arguments to Windows APIs
Faulty RAM or a failing disk returning scrambled data (rarer, but worth checking when failures look random)

fixes.title: Recheck the command syntax
fixes.detail: Pull up the tool's help (for example `dism /?` or `robocopy /?`) and compare each switch you used. Put quotes around any path that has spaces, as in `robocopy "C:\source dir" "D:\dest dir" /E`.

fixes.title: Repair system files with SFC
fixes.detail: Run `sfc /scannow` in an elevated Command Prompt. Restart when it's done and repeat the action that gave you error 87.

fixes.title: Repair the component store with DISM
fixes.detail: From an elevated prompt run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`. If DISM itself returns error 87, your build is probably older than that switch, so install all pending Windows Updates or do an in-place upgrade repair instead.

fixes.title: Check memory with Windows Memory Diagnostic
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe`, choose to restart and check for problems, and let the test run to the end. Bad memory can corrupt parameters as they pass between programs and the kernel, which would explain random error 87 failures.

fixes.title: Clean boot to isolate third-party software
fixes.detail: Open `msconfig`, hide all Microsoft services, disable everything else along with startup apps, then restart and try again. If error 87 goes away, turn items back on in groups until you find the program responsible.

prevention: Stay current on Windows Updates so newer tool switches are available
Copy commands from reliable sources rather than typing them from memory
Keep folder names free of unusual characters and trailing spaces
Make a restore point before running scripts that change system settings

title: ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND (The specified module could not be found)
codes: The specified module could not be found
summary: Error 126, 'The specified module could not be found', appears when Windows or an app tries to load a DLL or driver that is missing, damaged, or relies on other files that can't be located.
meaning: ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND is raised when LoadLibrary fails to load a module. Either the DLL isn't there, it was quarantined, or it depends on a second DLL that can't be found. Error 2 covers files in general, but error 126 is specific to loadable modules like DLLs and drivers, and it usually appears as a service or application is starting up.
commonCauses: A DLL that was deleted, quarantined by antivirus, or replaced with the wrong version
Registry Run keys or a service's ImagePath still pointing at a module that's been removed
The folder holding a dependent DLL isn't listed in the PATH environment variable
Missing Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable runtimes (x86 or x64)
A 32-bit program trying to load a 64-bit DLL, or the reverse

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the app
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > Apps > Installed apps and choose Modify or Repair, or launch the vendor's installer and select Repair. This puts the module back and registers it properly.

fixes.title: Install current Visual C++ Redistributables
fixes.detail: From Microsoft's 'latest supported VC++ downloads' page, install both the x86 and x64 Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable packages, then restart. Missing runtimes are behind a lot of error 126 launch failures.

fixes.title: Get the module back from quarantine
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history. Restore any quarantined DLL that belongs to software you trust, and add a folder exclusion for that app.

fixes.title: Run SFC and DISM when the module is part of Windows
fixes.detail: If the missing module is a Windows component, open an elevated prompt and run `sfc /scannow`, then `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`.

fixes.title: Find the conflicting software with a clean boot
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, select Selective startup, hide Microsoft services and disable the remaining third-party ones, then restart and test. Turn items back on a few at a time to see which program is loading the broken module.

prevention: Uninstall programs the proper way rather than deleting their folders
Keep Visual C++ Redistributables and .NET runtimes installed and up to date
Skip registry cleaners and 'DLL fixer' tools
Keep antivirus current to cut down on false positives against shared DLLs

title: 0x8007007E: ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND (apps and services)
summary: An app or service won't start and reports 0x8007007E, the HRESULT version of 'The specified module could not be found'. A DLL it needs at launch couldn't be loaded.
meaning: 0x8007007E is Win32 error 126 (ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND) expressed as an HRESULT. Something the program needs at launch, either a DLL or a driver, is missing, damaged or blocked. You'll run into it when starting desktop programs, Store apps or Windows services, typically after an install or update that didn't finish, an antivirus quarantine, or a service whose registration is broken. If you hit this code while installing updates, the separate update-focused 0x8007007e entry in the Windows Update section covers that case.
commonCauses: A needed DLL is gone after an unfinished install or an interrupted update
Antivirus quarantined a component the app or service uses
The service's ImagePath or registration refers to a module that was removed or renamed
A runtime dependency is missing or the wrong bitness (for example the VC++ redistributable)
The application's installed files are damaged

fixes.title: Reboot and launch the app or service again
fixes.detail: Restart the PC and try once more. File replacements left pending by an interrupted install frequently finish during the next boot.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the app
fixes.detail: In Settings > Apps > Installed apps, choose Modify or Repair, or reinstall from a freshly downloaded installer. For a Store app, open its Advanced options from the same list and try Repair first, then Reset.

fixes.title: Bring back quarantined files with Windows Security
fixes.detail: Go to Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history. Restore any quarantined component that belongs to trusted software, and exclude its folder.

fixes.title: Run SFC and DISM
fixes.detail: When a Windows component or service is the one failing, open an elevated prompt, run `sfc /scannow` and then `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`, and restart afterward.

fixes.title: Examine the failing service's configuration
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt, run `sc qc ServiceName` (substituting the real service name) and confirm the file shown in BINARY_PATH_NAME actually exists. If it doesn't, reinstall the software that owns the service instead of editing the registry manually.
fixes.riskNote: Leave service registry values alone unless you're sure of the correct path. A wrong ImagePath can stop the service, and the app that depends on it, from ever starting.

prevention: Don't shut down while installations or updates are still running
Keep Visual C++ Redistributables and .NET runtimes up to date
Don't delete shared DLLs or 'clean up' system folders by hand
Set up antivirus exclusions for development folders and trusted app folders

title: ERROR_SERVICE_DEPENDENCY_FAIL (Error 1068)
codes: The dependency service or group failed to start
summary: Error 1068 tells you a service couldn't start because another service it relies on failed to start first. Windows Audio, WLAN AutoConfig and Print Spooler are frequent examples.
meaning: Many Windows services are linked in dependency chains, and a service only starts once everything it depends on is running. If one of those prerequisites is disabled, broken or missing, the Service Control Manager stops the whole chain and reports error 1068. This often happens after 'service optimizer' tweaks, a malware cleanup, or a registry cleaner that switched off required services.
commonCauses: A prerequisite service was disabled by hand, by an optimization script or by a 'gaming' tweak
Malware removal or a registry cleaner damaged the service configuration
The dependency service is missing a driver or file it needs
A vendor support service (printer, audio suite, VPN) broke after a partial uninstall
Group policy or a third-party suite set the wrong startup types

fixes.title: Reboot and try the service again
fixes.detail: Restart the PC, then open services.msc, right-click the service and choose Start. Some dependency failures come from temporary locks that are gone after a reboot.

fixes.title: Inspect the service's dependencies
fixes.detail: In services.msc, open the failing service's Properties and switch to the Dependencies tab. Make sure every service listed there exists and isn't Disabled. Set those prerequisites to Manual or Automatic, start them beginning at the bottom of the chain, and then start the service that failed.

fixes.title: Put startup types back to their defaults
fixes.detail: If a tweaking tool switched services off, return each prerequisite to its standard Windows startup type (Windows Audio Endpoint Builder, for example, should be Automatic). Make a restore point before you change service settings.

fixes.title: Run SFC to repair damaged Windows services
fixes.detail: From an elevated prompt, run `sfc /scannow`. If it reports corruption, also run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`, then restart.

fixes.title: Reinstall the software or driver that owns the dependency
fixes.detail: When the prerequisite belongs to an app or driver (such as a printer suite, an audio driver or a VPN client), repair or reinstall it so its services are registered correctly again.

prevention: Don't run one-click 'disable all services' scripts on a PC you rely on
Make a restore point before changing any service's startup type
Keep real-time malware protection on so services can't be tampered with
Remove vendor suites completely with their uninstaller instead of deleting their services

title: ERROR_SERVICE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT (Error 1053)
codes: The service did not respond to the start or control request in a timely fashion
summary: Error 1053 shows up when a service is too slow to answer Windows' start request and the Service Control Manager stops waiting: 'The service did not respond to the start or control request in a timely fashion.'
meaning: Each time a service starts, the Service Control Manager gives the process a window (30 seconds by default) to report that it is up and running. If the executable stalls because it's waiting on a network resource that isn't there, lacks a runtime it needs, or is deadlocked, the request times out and you get error 1053. It's especially common with .NET services running on the wrong runtime, with antivirus agents, and with services that block while waiting for a network share or database.
commonCauses: The service executable freezes during startup (a deadlock or a resource that isn't available)
A missing or mismatched runtime, for example the wrong .NET version
A damaged service install left by a partial update or uninstall
A heavily loaded system or a slow disk pushing startup past the timeout
A network share or database the service needs is offline

fixes.title: Reboot and start the service once more
fixes.detail: Restart, then try again from services.msc. If the service starts fine after the reboot, think about what was different at the last shutdown (an update, a VPN, a mapped network drive), since that hints at the dependency.

fixes.title: Find the underlying failure in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Open Event Viewer and check Windows Logs > Application and System around the time of the failure. .NET runtime errors or crash reports from the service's executable usually reveal what's missing.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the app that owns the service
fixes.detail: Run the vendor's installer in Repair mode, or uninstall the application and install it again. That registers the service and its runtime dependencies correctly.

fixes.title: Clean boot to rule out third-party conflicts
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, turn off non-Microsoft services and startup apps, restart, and test the service. Turn things back on in groups to track down the conflict.

fixes.title: Run SFC and DISM for built-in Windows services
fixes.detail: If the service timing out is part of Windows (Windows Update or BITS, for instance), run `sfc /scannow` and `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` from an elevated prompt.

fixes.title: Raise the service timeout in the registry (last resort)
fixes.detail: As an advanced workaround for services that are legitimately slow, create a DWORD named `ServicesPipeTimeout` under `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control`, set it in milliseconds (180000, for example), and reboot.
fixes.riskNote: A wrong registry edit can break Windows, so back up the registry first and save this for last. A slow service usually signals a deeper problem that deserves a real fix.

prevention: Keep apps and the runtimes they use (.NET, VC++) up to date
Leave network services that your apps depend on enabled
Keep the disk healthy and with enough free space so service startup isn't delayed
Make a restore point before installing agent or server-style software

title: 0x80070570: ERROR_FILE_CORRUPT
codes: The file or directory is corrupted and unreadable
summary: 0x80070570 reads 'The file or directory is corrupted and unreadable'. Windows ran into real file-system corruption while installing, copying or reading files.
meaning: 0x80070570 is the HRESULT version of Win32 error 1392, ERROR_FILE_CORRUPT. Windows tried to read or write and found file-system structures or file contents that no longer make sense: broken NTFS metadata, sectors that can't be read, or data that got corrupted on the way. If you see it while installing or upgrading Windows, the install media is frequently the thing that's damaged.
commonCauses: Bad sectors, or a hard drive or SSD that is starting to fail
NTFS damage from an unclean shutdown or a sudden loss of power
Faulty installation media, such as a bad USB stick or an ISO that downloaded incorrectly
Defective RAM corrupting data as it's copied or written
Loose or worn cables on internal or external drives

fixes.title: Back up your important files first
fixes.detail: Before trying any repair, copy files you can't replace to another drive or to cloud storage. Corruption can be an early warning of drive failure, so secure your data before going further.

fixes.title: Run chkdsk on the drive
fixes.detail: Open an elevated Command Prompt and run `chkdsk C: /f /r`, swapping C: for the affected drive letter. On the system drive, accept the offer to run it at the next restart and let it complete.
fixes.riskNote: chkdsk puts heavy load on a weak drive and can sometimes turn borderline sectors unreadable, so finish your backup before you start it.

fixes.title: Run SFC and DISM when Windows files are involved
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `sfc /scannow`, then `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`, and restart.

fixes.title: Make new installation media (setup failures)
fixes.detail: If the error appears while installing or upgrading Windows, download the ISO again with the Media Creation Tool and write it to a different USB stick that you know is good.

fixes.title: Check RAM with Windows Memory Diagnostic
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe`, restart, and allow the extended test to finish. Bad memory is a well-known reason files end up corrupted as they're written.

fixes.title: Check drive health and replace a failing drive
fixes.detail: Look at the SMART status using the drive maker's utility or CrystalDiskInfo. If corruption keeps coming back, or you see pending or reallocated sectors, replace the drive and restore from your backup.

prevention: Run automatic backups following the 3-2-1 rule so corruption never costs you data
Always shut down properly, and use a UPS if your power is unreliable
Keep an eye on SMART health for both system and backup drives
Verify ISO downloads and write installers to good-quality USB sticks

title: ERROR_WRITE_PROTECT: Write-protected media (Error 1310)
summary: Error 1310 tells you Windows wanted to save data to a drive that only allows reading. The message reads 'The media is write protected', and the usual suspect is an SD card, a USB flash drive, or a disk that has locked itself into read-only mode.
meaning: Windows blocked the write because the destination refuses changes. That refusal can come from a mechanical lock switch, a read-only attribute set in software, or the drive's own firmware, which may go read-only on purpose to preserve whatever data is still readable. When an installer hits the same condition, you may instead see 'Error writing to file' because the target folder or device will not accept new data.
commonCauses: The lock tab on an SD card (or its adapter) is pushed to the Lock position
A USB stick with a built-in write-protect switch, or protection enforced by its firmware
A read-only flag applied to the disk through diskpart's 'attributes disk' command
Worn flash memory or an internal fault that caused the firmware to fall back to read-only
Security software or a group policy that blocks writing to removable storage

fixes.title: Inspect the card or drive for a lock switch
fixes.detail: Pull the SD card out and push its small lock tab all the way up toward the gold contacts, which is the unlocked position. Some USB flash drives also have a tiny write-protect slider on the side of the casing, so check for one.

fixes.title: Remove the read-only flag using diskpart
fixes.detail: Open Command Prompt as administrator and type `diskpart`. Run `list disk`, identify your device, then run `select disk N` followed by `attributes disk clear readonly`. Enter `exit` and try saving to the drive again.
fixes.riskNote: Confirm the disk number by its size before you select it. Picking the wrong number means you change the attributes of a different drive.

fixes.title: Test with a different port, reader, or computer
fixes.detail: Move the device to another USB port or card reader, or try it on a second PC. A loose or unreliable connection can make some readers report the media as write protected when it is not.

fixes.title: Look at device-control policies and security tools
fixes.detail: Find out whether your antivirus or a device-control product is locking removable drives to read-only. On a work or school PC, ask IT whether a group policy is applying the restriction.

fixes.title: Copy your data off and retire a drive that went read-only on its own
fixes.detail: When a drive that used to accept writes suddenly turns read-only without anyone changing a setting, treat it as a warning and copy its contents somewhere safe right away. Firmware usually does this to shield a worn-out drive, so plan on replacing it.
fixes.riskNote: A drive that switched itself to read-only is often near the end of its life. Do not store anything new on it.

prevention: Only move the SD card lock tab when you mean to, and keep cards in protective cases
Use Safely Remove Hardware rather than pulling a drive while it is writing
Keep a second copy of anything important that lives on removable media
Retire flash drives as soon as they start showing occasional write failures

title: 0x8007045D: ERROR_IO_DEVICE (I/O device error)
codes: The request could not be performed because of an I/O device error
summary: 0x8007045D, shown as 'I/O device error', means a disk could not finish a read or write at the hardware level. You will most often run into it while copying large files, installing software, running a backup, or setting up Windows.
meaning: The code is a wrapped form of Win32 error 1117 (ERROR_IO_DEVICE), which says the storage device, or the link to it, failed to complete a request. This is different from ordinary file corruption: it points to the physical side of things, such as bad sectors, a dying drive, a faulty USB cable or enclosure, or a SATA connector that has worked loose. If it keeps coming back, suspect hardware.
commonCauses: A hard drive or SSD that is failing or has bad or pending sectors
A worn or defective USB cable, external enclosure, or card reader
A SATA data or power cable that is not fully seated on an internal drive
Storage or USB controller drivers that are old or buggy
A corrupted installation USB when the error shows up during Windows setup

fixes.title: Get your data off the drive first
fixes.detail: Before trying anything else, copy your important files to a different drive or to cloud storage. Drives that throw I/O errors can stop working entirely with little warning.

fixes.title: Rule out the cable, port, and enclosure
fixes.detail: With an external drive, switch to another USB port and a cable you know works, or take the disk out of its enclosure and connect it over SATA as a test. With an internal drive, unplug and firmly reconnect both the SATA and power cables.

fixes.title: Scan the drive with chkdsk
fixes.detail: Open Command Prompt as administrator and run `chkdsk D: /f /r`, substituting the correct drive letter for D:. It repairs file system damage where it can and marks bad sectors so Windows stops using them.
fixes.riskNote: chkdsk puts a heavy load on the disk, which can push already failing hardware over the edge. Back up beforehand and stop the scan if the drive starts disconnecting.

fixes.title: Refresh storage and USB controller drivers
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager and update the drivers under Disk drives and the storage or USB controllers, or install the chipset package from your PC or motherboard maker. Restart and run the transfer again.

fixes.title: Rebuild the installation USB (during Windows setup)
fixes.detail: If setup is where the error appears, use the Media Creation Tool to write the ISO onto a different flash drive, and try another port. On older motherboards a USB 2.0 port is often more reliable.

fixes.title: Check drive health and replace it if needed
fixes.detail: Read the SMART data with the manufacturer's utility or CrystalDiskInfo. Reallocated or pending sectors, or errors that follow the drive no matter which cable or port you use, mean it is time for a new drive and a restore from backup.

prevention: Buy decent cables and enclosures instead of cheap unbranded adapters
Eject external drives properly and never disconnect them mid-copy
Run scheduled backups and keep an eye on SMART health readings
Keep the case well ventilated, since drives that run hot wear out sooner

title: ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND (The system cannot find the path specified)
codes: The system cannot find the path specified
summary: Error 3, 'The system cannot find the path specified', means some folder along the route to a file is missing or out of reach. Compare that with error 2, where the folders are fine and only the file itself is gone.
meaning: Windows returns ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND when it cannot follow a path all the way through: a folder in the middle no longer exists, the drive letter is wrong, or a network location will not respond. Typical sources include mapped drives that have dropped, a NAS share that is offline, app settings still pointing at a deleted folder, and PATH entries that name directories that have since been removed.
commonCauses: A mistyped folder name or the wrong drive letter in a path or command
A mapped network drive or NAS share that was disconnected or renamed
A folder that was moved, renamed, or deleted while programs still point to it
Entries in the PATH environment variable for folders that are gone
An external or secondary drive that came back with a different letter after being reconnected or after a reinstall

fixes.title: Confirm every folder in the path is really there
fixes.detail: Browse down the path one level at a time in File Explorer, or check it in Command Prompt with `dir "C:\first\second"`. Correcting a typo or a wrong drive letter fixes the majority of cases.

fixes.title: Bring the mapped network drive back
fixes.detail: In File Explorer, open This PC and look at the status of the mapped drive. Map it again with Map network drive, or from a command prompt run `net use Z: \\server\share /persistent:yes`. Also make sure the server or NAS is powered on and reachable.

fixes.title: Point the app at the correct folder
fixes.detail: Open the program's settings and update any stored locations, such as the default save folder, library path, or project directory. If those settings cannot be reached or fixed, reinstalling the app resets them.

fixes.title: Put the missing folder back
fixes.detail: If you deleted a folder that something still needs, create it again at the exact path expected, or bring it back from a backup. You can also right-click the parent folder and choose Restore previous versions.

fixes.title: Remove dead PATH entries (for command-line errors)
fixes.detail: Search for 'Edit the system environment variables', click Environment Variables, and delete any PATH entries that point to folders that no longer exist. Close and reopen any terminal windows afterward.
fixes.riskNote: Leave alone any PATH entry you do not recognize. Plenty of tools stop working if their folder disappears from PATH.

prevention: Give external drives fixed letters in Disk Management so they do not shift
Keep NAS shares available, or set mapped drives to reconnect when you sign in
Write down any custom folder layouts that your scripts and apps depend on
Run scripts with full absolute paths before you put them on a schedule

title: ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED
summary: ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED appears in Chrome and Edge, under 'This site can't be reached', when your connection shifted while a page was loading. Because the IP address or route changed partway through, the browser gave up on the request.
meaning: The operating system reported a change in network state during the transfer, so the browser cancelled what it was doing. Triggers include picking up a new DHCP lease, Wi-Fi hopping to a different access point, plugging in Ethernet, or a VPN reconnecting. Seeing it once is nothing to worry about. Seeing it often suggests an unstable adapter, overly aggressive power saving, or unreliable DHCP or VPN behavior.
commonCauses: Wi-Fi switching between access points or between the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands
A DHCP renewal handing out a different IP address during a session
A VPN client dropping and reconnecting, or moving to another server
Power management shutting off the network adapter to save battery
Bugs in the network adapter driver following a Windows or driver update

fixes.title: Refresh the page
fixes.detail: Press F5, or Ctrl+F5 for a hard refresh. In most cases the error was a one-time timing issue during a connection change and the page loads fine the second time.

fixes.title: Clear the DNS cache
fixes.detail: In Command Prompt, run `ipconfig /flushdns` and then reload the page. That removes cached lookups that may be out of date after your IP address changed.

fixes.title: Get a fresh IP address
fixes.detail: Run `ipconfig /release` and then `ipconfig /renew` in Command Prompt to request a new lease, and reload the page once it completes.

fixes.title: Keep Windows from switching the adapter off
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager, go to your Wi-Fi or Ethernet adapter, and on the Power Management tab clear 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'. That prevents the repeated drops that set off this error.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: From an elevated Command Prompt, run `netsh winsock reset` and then `netsh int ip reset`, and restart the PC. These commands rebuild the Winsock catalog and the TCP/IP settings if a driver or program damaged them.
fixes.riskNote: Afterward you may have to enter static IP details again and reconfigure some VPN or LSP-based software.

fixes.title: Reinstall the network adapter driver
fixes.detail: In Device Manager, right-click the adapter and choose Uninstall device. Only tick the option to delete the driver if you already have the vendor's driver on hand. Restart so Windows reinstalls it, or install the newest driver from your laptop or motherboard maker.

prevention: Get network drivers from the hardware maker instead of relying only on Windows Update
Turn off aggressive power saving for the network adapter on laptops
Use a solid 5 GHz signal or a wired connection for long sessions
Keep VPN software up to date, since outdated TAP drivers reconnect frequently

title: ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED
summary: ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED shows up when Windows itself has no internet connection. The browser is simply passing along the fact that the PC is offline.
meaning: The problem sits below the browser, at the operating system's connection. Wi-Fi may be off or airplane mode on, the Ethernet cable may be out, the adapter may be disabled, or the router, modem, or ISP line may be down. Since the browser is not at fault, restoring the connection is what makes the page load.
commonCauses: Wi-Fi turned off, airplane mode switched on, or a physical wireless switch flipped
A router or modem that is offline, frozen, or still restarting
An Ethernet cable that is unplugged or damaged
A network adapter that has been disabled or whose driver crashed
A service outage from your internet provider

fixes.title: Check Wi-Fi, airplane mode, and cables
fixes.detail: Press Win+A to open quick settings and make sure Wi-Fi is on, airplane mode is off, and your network says connected. On a wired PC, check that the Ethernet cable clicks into place at both ends and that the port lights are lit.

fixes.title: Power cycle the modem and router
fixes.detail: Pull the power from the modem and router, wait about 30 seconds, and plug them back in. Give them 2-3 minutes to fully start before you reconnect.

fixes.title: Use the built-in network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters, find Internet Connections, click Run, and accept any fixes it suggests.

fixes.title: Reset the network configuration
fixes.detail: Open an elevated Command Prompt and run `ipconfig /release`, `ipconfig /renew`, `netsh winsock reset`, and `netsh int ip reset` in that order. Then restart the computer.
fixes.riskNote: You may need to re-enter any custom IP or DNS settings after the reset.

fixes.title: Reinstall the network adapter driver
fixes.detail: Right-click the adapter in Device Manager, choose Uninstall device, and restart so Windows sets it up again. If the adapter vanishes completely afterward, download the vendor's driver on another device and bring it over on a USB stick.

fixes.title: Find out whether your provider is down
fixes.detail: Use a phone on mobile data to check your ISP's status page. If other devices at home are offline too, the outage is likely on the provider's end, so wait for service to return rather than changing settings on the PC.

prevention: Keep your network adapter driver on a USB stick in case you ever need it offline
Keep router firmware updated and use WPA2 or WPA3 with stable settings
Skip third-party 'network optimizer' tools that tamper with adapter settings
Bookmark your ISP's outage page on your phone

title: DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN
summary: DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN means the DNS lookup came back empty: the domain name could not be turned into an IP address, so from your PC's point of view the site does not exist.
meaning: NXDOMAIN is short for 'non-existent domain', the answer your DNS server gave when asked about the name. Either the address was typed wrong, or the resolver you are using (your ISP, your router, a VPN, or a public DNS service) is misconfigured, filtering, or failing. In most cases the website itself is up, which you can check from a different device or network.
commonCauses: ISP DNS servers that are malfunctioning or overloaded
A spelling mistake in the domain name
A VPN, proxy, or security product that intercepts DNS requests
An outdated local DNS cache after the site moved to new hosting
A router with bad DNS forwarding settings or a corrupted cache

fixes.title: Double-check the address and test on another device
fixes.detail: Read the address carefully, letter by letter, then try opening the site on your phone or another computer. If it fails on every device, the issue is with the site or its DNS records rather than your PC.

fixes.title: Clear the DNS cache
fixes.detail: Run `ipconfig /flushdns` in Command Prompt and reload the page.

fixes.title: Use a public DNS service
fixes.detail: Open your adapter settings, go to Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) > Properties, choose to enter DNS servers manually, and use 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 (1.0.0.1 and 8.8.4.4 also work as alternates). For IPv6, the equivalents are 2606:4700:4700::1111 and 2001:4860:4860::8888.

fixes.title: Renew the IP lease
fixes.detail: In Command Prompt, run `ipconfig /release` followed by `ipconfig /renew` so the PC picks up a fresh lease and DNS settings from the router.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and reboot
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` from an elevated Command Prompt and then restart. This clears out damaged Winsock entries that VPNs and security filters sometimes leave behind.

fixes.title: Test without the VPN and proxy
fixes.detail: Disconnect your VPN, then open Settings > Network & internet > Proxy and make sure no leftover proxy is configured. Try the site again.

prevention: Use a dependable public DNS service (1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8) if your ISP connection is unreliable
Restart the router now and then and keep its firmware current
Update VPN and proxy software to avoid bugs that intercept DNS
Stay away from DNS 'accelerator' programs

title: ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED
summary: ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED is the browser's catch-all message for a DNS failure. None of the DNS servers your PC uses managed to turn the site name into an address.
meaning: NXDOMAIN is a firm 'this name does not exist' reply. ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED is broader and covers any lookup that failed, whether it timed out, was refused, or broke because of a configuration problem. Frequent causes are DNS servers that are not working, VPN split-tunnel mistakes, overrides in the hosts file, and security software that filters DNS traffic.
commonCauses: The configured DNS server (from your ISP or set manually) is down or not responding
A VPN or proxy setup that interferes with name resolution
Lines in the hosts file that redirect or block the domain
IPv6 problems that make AAAA lookups hang and stall the page
Security suites or parental controls that intercept DNS queries

fixes.title: Clear the DNS cache
fixes.detail: Open Command Prompt, run `ipconfig /flushdns`, and reload the page.

fixes.title: Change DNS to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8
fixes.detail: In the adapter's IPv4 properties, set the DNS servers manually to 1.1.1.1 with 8.8.8.8 as the alternate, or configure the router to use them. Then reload the page.

fixes.title: Look for overrides in the hosts file
fixes.detail: Run Notepad as administrator and open C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts. Delete any lines for the failing domain that you did not add yourself, or disable them by putting # at the start.
fixes.riskNote: Change only lines you understand. Developers and security tools also use the hosts file for valid redirects.

fixes.title: Turn off the proxy and try without the VPN
fixes.detail: Disconnect from any VPN. Then go to Settings > Network & internet > Proxy and confirm 'Use a proxy server' is turned off, unless your network actually requires a proxy. Load the site again.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and restart
fixes.detail: From an elevated Command Prompt, run `netsh winsock reset`, then restart the PC. This rebuilds the network service stack if a filter driver damaged it.

prevention: Add a comment and a date next to any hosts-file change you make
Keep your VPN client updated and set up split tunneling on purpose, not by accident
Keep a public DNS server configured as a backup
Fully uninstall proxy or filtering software you no longer use instead of just disabling it

title: 0x800704CF: The network location cannot be reached
codes: The network location cannot be reached
summary: 0x800704CF, 'The network location cannot be reached', appears when a program cannot get onto the network. VPN clients and Microsoft account sign-ins are common places to see it, and Windows often shows 'Unidentified network' at the same time.
meaning: This code wraps Win32 error 1231 (ERROR_NETWORK_UNREACHABLE). The adapter is active, but Windows has no working route to where it needs to go, usually because the default gateway or DNS settings are missing or the TCP/IP stack is damaged. It is a familiar sight with VPN software (particularly leftover TAP or virtual adapters), after network driver updates, and on PCs that report 'Unidentified network' even though the cable is fine.
commonCauses: A missing default gateway or failed DHCP setup, shown as 'Unidentified network'
Old or conflicting VPN virtual adapters (TAP) left by previous clients
TCP/IP or Winsock corruption after a driver update or a malware cleanup
A third-party firewall or security suite that blocks routing
A Windows update that introduced a driver or network profile bug

fixes.title: Turn the adapter off and on, then run the troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Switch Wi-Fi or Ethernet off and back on from quick settings. Then open Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters, find Network Adapter, and click Run.

fixes.title: Request a new IP address
fixes.detail: Open Command Prompt as administrator and run `ipconfig /release`, `ipconfig /renew`, and `ipconfig /flushdns`. Then run `ipconfig /all` and confirm a valid default gateway is listed.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: From an elevated prompt, run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset`, then restart. Repairing the protocol stack this way is the usual remedy for error 1231.
fixes.riskNote: Afterward you may need to set up static IP, DNS, and VPN settings again.

fixes.title: Clean out leftover VPN adapters
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager > Network adapters and uninstall virtual adapters that belong to VPN software you have already removed (for example, old TAP-Windows entries). Restart when done.
fixes.riskNote: Remove only adapters you can tie to uninstalled software. Taking out an adapter that a VPN still uses will stop that VPN from working.

fixes.title: Reinstall the network adapter driver
fixes.detail: Uninstall the physical network adapter in Device Manager, deleting the driver too if you already have the vendor installer downloaded. Restart, then install the newest driver from the manufacturer.

prevention: Remove old VPN clients completely rather than piling several on one PC
Install network drivers from the hardware manufacturer
Avoid third-party firewalls that quietly change routing rules
Restart the router after ISP changes so leases and gateways refresh properly

title: 0xc0000225: A required device isn't connected or can't be accessed
codes: A required device isn't connected or can't be accessed
Your PC needs to be repaired
summary: 0xc0000225 shows up on a blue recovery screen during startup with the message 'A required device isn't connected or can't be accessed'. It means Windows Boot Manager cannot get to something it needs in order to boot.
meaning: The boot manager went looking for Windows in a place it can no longer reach. Maybe the BCD refers to a partition that moved or no longer exists, the disk disappeared, or the EFI or system partition is damaged. Common triggers include an update that failed, an abrupt power cut, changes to disks, and switching storage or firmware modes in the BIOS.
commonCauses: BCD entries that are corrupted or out of date after a failed update or forced shutdown
A failing disk or a loose data or power cable
A BIOS storage mode change (RAID to AHCI or back) or a firmware mode change (UEFI to Legacy or back)
A damaged EFI System Partition or System Reserved partition
Partition changes made while setting up dual boot or cloning a disk

fixes.title: Let Startup Repair try first
fixes.detail: From the recovery screen, go to Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair and allow it to finish. If the recovery environment does not appear, interrupt startup three times in a row (turn the PC off while the dots spin), or boot from a Windows installation USB and pick 'Repair your computer'.

fixes.title: Rebuild the BCD using bootrec
fixes.detail: Open Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Command Prompt and run `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. For MBR disks, also run `bootrec /fixmbr`, and run `bootrec /fixboot` to rewrite the boot sector. Restart and see whether Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: These commands overwrite boot code. If /fixboot returns 'Access is denied', which happens often on UEFI systems, move on to the bcdboot step instead of running it again.

fixes.title: Recreate the boot files with bcdboot (advanced)
fixes.detail: In the WinRE command prompt, start `diskpart`, use list volume and select volume to find the EFI partition, and give it a letter with `assign letter=S`. Exit diskpart and run `bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI`, using whichever letter WinRE gives the Windows volume. Remove the temporary letter and restart.
fixes.riskNote: Using the wrong drive letter, or formatting the EFI partition, can leave the PC unable to start. Work through an up-to-date guide one step at a time and never quick format a volume you cannot identify.

fixes.title: Review the boot order and storage mode in firmware
fixes.detail: Open the BIOS or UEFI setup and make sure the Windows drive is first in the boot order, and that the storage mode (AHCI or RAID), boot mode (UEFI or Legacy), and Secure Boot setting are the same as before the problem started.
fixes.riskNote: Write down the current firmware settings before touching anything. Switching modes incorrectly can hide the disk from the boot process.

fixes.title: Scan the disk from the recovery environment
fixes.detail: In the recovery command prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f /r`, replacing C: with the letter WinRE shows for the Windows drive. Wait for it to finish, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore an image or reinstall Windows (last resort)
fixes.detail: If nothing else works, restore a system image backup or use installation media to reinstall Windows while keeping personal files. Before you do, copy important data to another drive using the WinRE command prompt or a Linux live USB.
fixes.riskNote: A reinstall can wipe data, so rescue your files before you begin.

prevention: Make a Windows recovery USB while the computer is still working
Let updates complete and do not force the power off during startup
Keep full image backups of the system drive
Do not change BIOS storage or firmware modes unless you know how to switch them back

title: 0xc000000f: Boot configuration data file is missing
codes: An error occurred while attempting to read the boot configuration data
summary: 0xc000000f during startup means Windows cannot read its Boot Configuration Data (BCD). Usually the \Boot\BCD file is missing or unreadable, which leaves the boot manager without an entry to start.
meaning: Windows Boot Manager tried to open the BCD store and failed, either because the file is gone, the boot partition is damaged, or the disk returned read errors. This often happens after a failed update, a forced shutdown, a change in BitLocker state, or when a disk starts to fail. You end up at the recovery screen with no automatic way into Windows.
commonCauses: A BCD store that was corrupted or deleted by a failed update or a power cut
A failing or disconnected disk that produces read errors during boot
Damage to the System Reserved or EFI boot partition
A boot sector harmed by disk utilities or cloning software
BitLocker recovery changes that left the boot chain out of sync

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair
fixes.detail: Get into the recovery environment, open Troubleshoot > Advanced options, and choose Startup Repair. If the first run says it made no changes, run it again, since it can rebuild basic boot entries.

fixes.title: Rebuild the BCD with bootrec
fixes.detail: Go to Advanced options > Command Prompt and run `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. If it detects a Windows installation, agree to add it. Then run `bootrec /fixmbr` (for MBR disks) and `bootrec /fixboot`.
fixes.riskNote: These commands rewrite boot code, so make a note of your disk and partition layout first. On UEFI systems, if /fixboot reports 'Access is denied', use bcdboot instead.

fixes.title: Create fresh boot files with bcdboot (advanced)
fixes.detail: Use diskpart to give the EFI or system partition a drive letter, then run `bcdboot C:\Windows`, or `bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI` when targeting an EFI partition. This writes new boot files along with a new BCD store.
fixes.riskNote: Drive letters in WinRE are often different from normal, so check them with `dir C:\` first. Writing to the wrong volume can damage that installation.

fixes.title: Scan the disk from WinRE
fixes.detail: In the recovery command prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f /r` to rule out disk errors, then try booting again.

fixes.title: Restore a system image or reinstall (last resort)
fixes.detail: If rebuilding the BCD does not help, restore a system image or reinstall Windows from installation media. Save your personal files somewhere else first.
fixes.riskNote: Reinstalling can lose data, so copy your files off before you start.

prevention: Keep a recovery USB and an up-to-date system image on hand
Shut down normally, and look into the cause of crashes instead of repeatedly holding the power button
Watch your disk's SMART health, because a failing disk can corrupt the BCD
Suspend BitLocker before you change boot settings or disk layout

title: Winload.efi is missing or corrupt (0xc0000098)
codes: The selected entry could not be loaded because the application is missing or corrupt
summary: The message 'Winload.efi is missing or corrupt' (0xc0000098) means the UEFI boot loader could not be loaded. Windows never begins starting, and the PC lands on the recovery screen instead.
meaning: On a UEFI PC, the boot manager passes control to \Windows\system32\winload.efi, which is the operating system loader. Status 0xc0000098 says that file is missing or damaged, or that the BCD is sending the boot manager to the wrong location. It typically follows a failed update, cloning a disk, resizing partitions, or damage to the EFI System Partition.
commonCauses: A BCD entry that points to the wrong partition after cloning or resizing
winload.efi damaged by an update that was interrupted or failed
Corrupted contents on the EFI System Partition (ESP)
Read errors on the disk that holds Windows
Hidden boot files removed by an overzealous cleanup tool

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair in the recovery environment
fixes.detail: Get into WinRE, either by booting an installation USB and choosing Repair your computer or by interrupting startup three times. Then go to Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair and let it finish. Run it a second time if necessary.

fixes.title: Rebuild the BCD with bootrec
fixes.detail: In the WinRE command prompt, run `bootrec /rebuildbcd`, followed by `bootrec /fixmbr` and `bootrec /fixboot` where they apply to your disk layout.
fixes.riskNote: Record the partition layout before you start. On UEFI machines, /fixboot often answers 'Access is denied', and the bcdboot step below takes care of that situation.

fixes.title: Restore the EFI boot files with bcdboot (advanced)
fixes.detail: Use diskpart to give the EFI partition an unused letter, confirm which volume holds Windows with `dir`, and then run `bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI`. This copies clean boot files, winload.efi included, and writes a BCD that matches them.
fixes.riskNote: Volume letters inside WinRE frequently differ from what you are used to, so check each one. Writing boot files to the wrong partition can break a Windows installation that was working.

fixes.title: Repair Windows files with an offline SFC scan
fixes.detail: From WinRE, run `sfc /scannow /offbootdir=C:\ /offwindir=C:\Windows`, adjusting the letters to match what WinRE shows. This fixes damaged system files. Then try booting again.

fixes.title: Check the disk, then restore or reinstall if needed
fixes.detail: Run `chkdsk C: /f /r` from WinRE. If the loader still cannot be fixed, save your personal files and then restore a system image or reinstall Windows while keeping files.
fixes.riskNote: Data loss is possible during a reinstall, so back up your files first.

prevention: Make a recovery USB before anything goes wrong
Do not interrupt updates, and keep the PC plugged in during feature upgrades
Use disk cloning tools carefully, and confirm the new disk boots before wiping the original
Keep image backups of the system drive

title: Device Manager Code 10: This device cannot start
summary: When Device Manager reports 'This device cannot start. (Code 10)', the driver did load, but it told Windows the hardware would not initialize. In most cases the driver and the device are not communicating properly.
meaning: Code 10 is a status Device Manager uses when a device's startup routine fails. Windows can see the hardware (so it is not listed as an unknown device), yet the driver could not get it running. Audio chips, USB devices, and graphics cards are frequent examples after a driver update. The underlying cause can be either the driver software or a real hardware fault.
commonCauses: A driver that is corrupt, outdated, or incompatible, often right after a Windows or driver update
Faulty hardware or a bad connection, such as a worn USB port or a loose card
Not enough power from a USB hub or the front-panel ports
Clashes with other drivers or with filter drivers installed by vendor software
Old BIOS or firmware on certain laptops and motherboards

fixes.title: Restart the computer
fixes.detail: A reboot can clear a device that got stuck in a bad state. Check Device Manager again once you are back in Windows.

fixes.title: Remove the device and scan again
fixes.detail: Right-click the device in Device Manager and select Uninstall device. If you are not sure about deleting the driver, leave that option unchecked. Then choose Action > Scan for hardware changes so Windows installs it again from scratch.

fixes.title: Install a newer driver
fixes.detail: Try Update driver in Device Manager, but you will usually get better results downloading the current driver from the device, laptop, or motherboard maker. Windows Update often delivers generic drivers that do not work well with every model.

fixes.title: Go back to the previous driver
fixes.detail: If the trouble began right after a driver update, open the device's Properties, go to the Driver tab, and click Roll Back Driver. Hold off on optional driver updates until a more stable release is available.

fixes.title: Try a different port or reseat the hardware
fixes.detail: Connect USB devices straight to a port on the back of the PC rather than through a hub. For expansion cards, shut down and reseat the card. Testing the device on another computer will tell you whether the hardware itself is bad.

prevention: Make a restore point before updating drivers
Use the manufacturer's drivers instead of generic Windows ones for important devices
Do not run beta drivers on PCs you depend on
Keep BIOS and firmware updated on laptops known for device startup problems

title: Device Manager Code 43: Windows has stopped this device
codes: Windows has stopped this device because it has reported problems
summary: 'Windows has stopped this device because it has reported problems. (Code 43)' means the hardware reported a failure and Windows switched it off. Graphics cards are the device most often affected by far.
meaning: Windows issues Code 43 when a device signals an error it cannot recover from. On a graphics card, that usually follows a driver crash, overheating, an unstable overclock or undervolt, a power shortfall, or an actual hardware failure in the memory or VRM. On a USB device, it more often points to faulty hardware, a bad cable, or too little power. The device stays disabled until whatever caused the fault is cleared.
commonCauses: A damaged or crashing graphics driver (the most typical case)
An unstable overclock or undervolt, including automatic factory OC tools
Overheating, a power supply without enough wattage, or aging power delivery
A real GPU hardware fault, such as failing VRAM or power stages
For USB Code 43: a faulty device, a bad cable, or a hub without its own power

fixes.title: Do a complete power drain
fixes.detail: Shut down fully and unplug the power cord. On a laptop, unplug the charger and, if you can, disconnect the battery. Hold the power button for 30 seconds to discharge, then reconnect and start up. This resets the card's power state and clears many temporary Code 43 errors.

fixes.title: Cleanly reinstall the graphics driver
fixes.detail: In Device Manager, uninstall the display adapter with 'Attempt to remove the driver for this device' selected, then restart and install the newest stable driver from NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel. Download the installer ahead of time so you have it available offline.

fixes.title: Return to the earlier driver
fixes.detail: If Code 43 started immediately after a driver update, go to Properties > Driver tab > Roll Back Driver, or reinstall the last version that worked reliably from the vendor's site.

fixes.title: Undo overclocks and undervolts
fixes.detail: Set MSI Afterburner or any other tuning tool back to stock settings, turn off automatic overclocking, and test again. A setup that seemed stable for months can start failing with Code 43 once a Windows update changes timing tolerances.

fixes.title: Inspect cooling and power delivery
fixes.detail: Blow the dust out of fans and heatsinks, make sure the GPU fans actually spin under load, and check that your power supply meets the card's requirements and uses good PCIe cables. Do not run a power-hungry card from a single daisy-chained cable.

fixes.title: Try the card in another computer
fixes.detail: If Code 43 remains with stock settings, clean hardware, correct power, and a fresh driver, test the GPU in a different PC or put another GPU in this one. If the error follows the card from system to system, it needs repair or replacement.

prevention: Stick with stable vendor driver releases and update on your own schedule rather than automatically
Overclock conservatively and run a stress test after every change
Choose a power supply with comfortable headroom above the card's peak draw
Clean dust out of the case and graphics card every few months

title: Windows cannot verify the digital signature (0xc0000428)
codes: Windows cannot verify the digital signature
summary: Windows will not load a driver or boot file if it cannot confirm the file's digital signature. This usually happens after installing an unsigned or outdated driver, or when the signing certificate has been revoked.
meaning: Kernel-mode drivers and boot components must have valid signatures before Windows will run them. Status 0xc0000428 (STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_HASH) stops any file whose signature is missing, invalid, or revoked. You will see it with older drivers, test-signed builds, and more and more often with drivers whose certificates Microsoft has revoked. If the blocked file is part of the boot process, the PC may not start at all.
commonCauses: An old or unsigned driver, for example for a legacy printer or older peripheral software
A driver signed with a certificate that was later revoked, as happened in the 2022 revocations
A corrupted driver file that fails its hash check
Secure Boot policy rejecting an outdated or modified boot component
A newly installed program that brings along an old kernel driver

fixes.title: Uninstall or roll back the driver you just added
fixes.detail: Work out which driver or program was installed right before the error started. Remove it through Settings > Apps, and remove the driver in Device Manager, or use Properties > Driver > Roll Back Driver. Then restart.

fixes.title: Get a currently signed driver from the manufacturer
fixes.detail: Download the newest driver package straight from the hardware maker and install it. Vendors re-sign their drivers after a revocation, so an older copy you saved yourself may still be blocked.
