fixes.detail: Right-click the app or terminal and choose Run as administrator. For scripts, open an elevated terminal first and launch them from there. A good share of 0x80070005 reports come down to a caller that simply was not elevated.

fixes.title: Look at antivirus and Controlled Folder Access
fixes.detail: In Windows Security, open Virus & threat protection > Manage ransomware protection > Controlled folder access. Check the block history and allow the app that was stopped. If you use third-party antivirus, check its quarantine and block logs too.

fixes.title: Repair Windows Update or Store permissions
fixes.detail: For Update errors, run `sfc /scannow` and `dism /online /cleanup-image /restorehealth`, then reset the update components (stop wuauserv and bits, and rename SoftwareDistribution). For Store errors, run `wsreset.exe`.

fixes.title: Take ownership of individual user folders, never system folders
fixes.detail: For one specific folder you cannot open, go to Properties > Security > Advanced, change the owner to your account and apply. Do NOT take ownership of C:\Windows or Program Files as a whole, because that permanently damages servicing.
fixes.riskNote: Sweeping permission changes on system folders lead to worse 0x80070005 errors down the road.

fixes.title: Review Group Policy and registry restrictions
fixes.detail: On work or school PCs, policy may deny certain actions; run `gpresult /h report.html` to see what applies. At home, look for leftovers from tweaking tools under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies, and either restore defaults or use a restore point.

prevention: Skip registry 'privacy tweakers' that rewrite system permissions
Allow specific apps in Controlled Folder Access instead of turning the feature off
Use one administrator account for system changes and a standard account day to day

title: CBS_E_STORE_CORRUPT (0x800f0831)
summary: Windows Update fails with 0x800f0831 because the component store (WinSxS) is too damaged for servicing to continue, and DISM may report corruption it cannot fix online.
meaning: 0x800f0831 comes from Component Based Servicing (CBS): files needed to install an update are missing from the component store or fail validation. Normally DISM /RestoreHealth sorts out store problems. When it fails with this same code, the local store is too broken to heal itself, and it needs a known-good repair source such as a mounted Windows ISO or Windows Update.
commonCauses: An interrupted update or power failure corrupting WinSxS files
Aggressive disk cleanup tools or 'debloat' scripts deleting component files
A failing drive losing writes to the component store
Servicing problems left unrepaired for months, piling up errors over time

fixes.title: Run DISM RestoreHealth using Windows Update as the source
fixes.detail: In an admin terminal, run `dism /online /cleanup-image /restorehealth` and let it run to the end, even if it seems to sit at 20% to 40% for a long time. Follow up with `sfc /scannow`, then try the update again.

fixes.title: Point DISM at a mounted Windows ISO
fixes.detail: Download the Windows 11 ISO from Microsoft, right-click it and choose Mount. Find the correct image index with `dism /get-wiminfo /wimfile:X:\sources\install.wim`, then run `dism /online /cleanup-image /restorehealth /source:WIM:X:\sources\install.wim:1 /limitaccess`, replacing X: with the mounted drive and 1 with your edition's index.

fixes.title: Install the update manually from the Update Catalog
fixes.detail: Get the failing KB from the Microsoft Update Catalog and install it yourself with `wusa.exe kbfile.msu` or `dism /online /add-package`. Supplying the payload locally sidesteps the damaged store path.

fixes.title: Run an in-place repair upgrade
fixes.detail: Mount the ISO, run setup.exe and choose to keep personal files and apps. Windows and its component store are rebuilt in place, which is the standard answer when DISM cannot repair the store.
fixes.riskNote: Make a backup first. An in-place upgrade is generally safe, but it is not risk-free on a drive that is failing.

prevention: Keep the PC plugged in during updates and never interrupt servicing
Avoid 'debloat' scripts that remove WinSxS components
Repair the store right away if DISM ever reports corruption it cannot fix, because the damage grows

title: 0x80073D05: Microsoft Store cache error
summary: The Microsoft Store will not open or install apps because its local cache or package data has become corrupted. Microsoft lists this code specifically as a Store cache problem.
meaning: With 0x80073D05, the Store ran into damaged temporary data, such as its download cache, its app registration or its AppX deployment state. You may see the Store crash as it opens, hang indefinitely on 'Getting a license', or reject every install until the cache is reset.
commonCauses: A corrupted Store download cache (exactly what WSReset is built to fix)
Store app registration broken by a Windows update
An incorrect date or time breaking the Store's secure connection
The AppX Deployment Service stalled partway through an update

fixes.title: Clear the Store cache with WSReset
fixes.detail: Press Win+R, enter `wsreset.exe` and press Enter. An empty console window appears; do not close it. After about 30 seconds it disappears and the Store reopens with a fresh cache. Your settings and installed apps are untouched.

fixes.title: Confirm date, time and region
fixes.detail: In Settings > Time & language > Date & time, turn on 'Set time automatically' and 'Set time zone automatically', then click Sync now. When the clock drifts, Store licensing can fail without a clear message.

fixes.title: Register the Store app again
fixes.detail: Close the Store, open PowerShell as administrator and run `Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers Microsoft.WindowsStore | Foreach {Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register "$($_.InstallLocation)\AppXManifest.xml"}`. It rebuilds the Store's package registration without reinstalling anything.
fixes.riskNote: Paste the command exactly as shown, because registering the wrong package path can cause additional AppX errors.

fixes.title: Run the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters and click Run next to Windows Store Apps. It checks the cache, licensing and related services for you.

fixes.title: Fix system files using DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: From an elevated Command Prompt, run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` and then `sfc /scannow`. Corrupted system components involved in AppX deployment are a known cause.

prevention: Give Store app updates time to finish before you shut down
Run WSReset now and then if installs begin to fail
Leave Windows Update turned on so Store services keep receiving fixes

title: Microsoft Store error 0x80073CF9 (app install failed)
summary: The app finishes downloading from the Microsoft Store, then the install step fails with 0x80073CF9. In most cases the problem is the install drive, the app's package registration, or damaged system components.
meaning: Store apps go through the AppX deployment pipeline, which stages the package on a drive and then registers it with Windows. Error 0x80073CF9 means that staging or registration could not be completed, usually because the target drive is full or unusable, the existing registration is corrupt, or system files are damaged. You typically see the progress bar reach the end, followed by the message 'This app couldn't be installed'.
commonCauses: The drive selected under 'New apps will save to' is full, disconnected or no longer valid
A broken package registration for the app you are installing, or for the Store itself
Corrupted AppX deployment components that DISM can repair
Windows Update services turned off, even though Store installs depend on them
An external or removable drive chosen as the app location that was later unplugged

fixes.title: Confirm where new apps are saved
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > System > Storage > Advanced storage settings > Where new content is saved. Set 'New apps will save to' to your Windows drive (normally C:) or to another healthy drive that has plenty of free space. Then try the install again.

fixes.title: Clear the Store cache using WSReset
fixes.detail: Open the Run box with Win+R, enter `wsreset.exe` and press Enter. A blank window appears briefly, then the Store reopens on its own. This wipes out corrupted staging data left between the download and install phases.

fixes.title: Restart the Windows Update service
fixes.detail: Because Store installs depend on a healthy, enabled Windows Update service, open Command Prompt as administrator and run `net stop wuauserv` followed by `net start wuauserv`, then reboot. If the service will not start, open `services.msc` and make sure Windows Update is not set to Disabled (a related symptom is error `0x80070422` when updating).

fixes.title: Run DISM and SFC to repair system files
fixes.detail: In an elevated Command Prompt, run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` and, once it completes, run `sfc /scannow`. Together they repair the deployment components Windows uses to register Store packages.

prevention: Leave at least 10% of the app install drive free
Keep Windows Update services enabled on any PC that uses the Store
Start big game installs only when the PC can stay on and plugged in until they finish

title: Activation error 0x8007007B (product key not valid)
summary: Windows will not accept the product key you typed. With 0x8007007B, the usual explanation is a typo, a key for a different edition, or a key that does not apply to this device.
meaning: During activation, 0x8007007B is the familiar 'invalid syntax' result. It tells you the key could not be matched to a valid Windows license for the edition and channel you have installed. Look-alike characters (0 and O, 1 and I, B and 8) are a frequent culprit, as are a Home key entered on a Pro installation and a key copied from the sticker on a different PC.
commonCauses: One or more characters mistyped in the 25-character key
A key meant for another edition, such as Home instead of Pro
A retail key that is already in use on a different computer
An OEM key embedded in firmware that no longer applies after major hardware changes

fixes.title: Type the key again, slowly
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Activation > Change product key. Enter the key one character at a time and watch for the classic mix-ups: 0 and O, 1 with I or L, and 8 with B. If you received the key by email, copy and paste it straight from the message.

fixes.title: Use the Activation troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > System > Activation > Troubleshoot. The tool checks again for a license embedded in firmware and can automatically reconnect a digital license that is linked to your Microsoft account.

fixes.title: Make sure the key and the installed edition match
fixes.detail: Check Settings > System > About to see which edition is installed. Home keys do not activate Pro, and Pro keys do not activate Home; that mismatch is reported as 0x8007007B. If the two differ, either install the edition your key covers or buy an upgrade through the Store.

fixes.title: Enter the key with SLUI or activate by phone
fixes.detail: Press Win+R and run `slui 3` to type in a new key. If online activation keeps failing, run `slui 4` to start phone activation instead. Phone activation is Microsoft's documented fallback and handles most edge cases around key validity.

prevention: Keep the product key with the PC's paperwork or saved in your Microsoft account
Purchase keys only from Microsoft or an authorized retailer
Link the Windows license to your Microsoft account so reactivation is painless

title: Activation error 0x803FA067 (digital license not found)
summary: Windows cannot locate a valid digital license or product key for this PC. It is the activation error people hit most often after replacing a motherboard or clean installing on hardware that used to activate without trouble.
meaning: With 0x803FA067, the activation servers report that no license matches this device's hardware hash. Either the PC never held a qualifying license, or its digital license is still tied to the old hardware fingerprint. That second case is typical after a motherboard replacement or after moving a drive into a different computer.
commonCauses: A motherboard or other core component was replaced and the license was never re-linked
Windows was clean installed without signing in to the Microsoft account that owns the digital license
The license is an OEM license that stays with the original machine
The installed edition is different from the one the license covers

fixes.title: Sign in with the Microsoft account used on the old install
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Accounts and sign in with the same account you used when Windows was last activated. A digital license linked to that account reactivates automatically as long as the hardware hash is similar enough.

fixes.title: Run the Activation troubleshooter and report a hardware change
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > System > Activation > Troubleshoot. If you rebuilt the PC recently, select 'I changed hardware on this device recently', sign in, and choose this device to move the license over. Microsoft documents this as the route to take after a motherboard swap.

fixes.title: Check that the edition matches the license
fixes.detail: In Settings > System > About, compare the 'Windows edition' value with the edition your key or license is for. If you installed Pro on a machine licensed for Home, 0x803FA067 will keep appearing until the editions line up.

fixes.title: Enter a valid key or activate by phone
fixes.detail: Press Win+R and run `slui 3` to type in a key you purchased, or `slui 4` to use the automated phone activation line. If the license is an OEM license that belongs to another PC, you will need a new license, since no tool can legally move it.

prevention: Link the Windows digital license to a Microsoft account (Settings > System > Activation)
Find out whether your license is retail or OEM before upgrading the motherboard
Keep your proof of purchase for the Windows license

title: Activation error 0xC004C003 (blocked product key)
summary: The activation server has flagged this product key as blocked. Microsoft disables keys like this, usually because they were abused, resold outside their terms, or leaked publicly.
meaning: Error 0xC004C003 is a decision made on Microsoft's servers. The key is recognized, but it is marked as blocked. That happens to volume license keys posted online, keys sold by gray-market resellers, and retail keys revoked after a chargeback. Nothing you do on the PC can remove the block.
commonCauses: A volume or KMS key used outside the terms of its licensing agreement
A key bought on the gray market, or resold secondhand after it was already activated
A key revoked because of a payment dispute or detected fraud
A typo that happens to turn your key into a different key that is blocked

fixes.title: Rule out a typo
fixes.detail: Press Win+R, run `slui 3` and enter the key again. If a mistyped character turned it into someone else's blocked key, entering your genuine key correctly solves the problem right away.

fixes.title: Use the Activation troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Activation > Troubleshoot. When a valid digital license is linked to your Microsoft account, Windows can activate from that license and skip the blocked key entirely.

fixes.title: Ask the seller for a replacement, or buy a genuine license
fixes.detail: If a reseller sold you the key, contact them, mention error 0xC004C003, and ask for a replacement or a refund. Otherwise, buy a genuine license from Microsoft or an authorized retailer. A blocked key cannot be repaired on your PC.

fixes.title: Confirm the block through phone activation
fixes.detail: Press Win+R, run `slui 4`, select your country or region, and call the number shown. The automated system tells you whether the key is permanently blocked and, if the key is usable, gives you a confirmation ID to activate.

prevention: Buy Windows keys only from Microsoft or authorized retailers
Assume that a marketplace key priced far below retail is likely to be blocked at some point
Save receipts and license documents in case you need to contact support

title: Windows Defender error 0x800106BA (Defender service will not start)
summary: Microsoft Defender Antivirus (Windows Defender) fails to start its service, so protection is either off or stuck initializing. A competing third-party antivirus or damaged security components are behind it almost every time.
meaning: Error 0x800106BA means the Defender service, or a service it depends on, did not initialize. Windows deliberately turns Defender off when another antivirus product registers with Security Center. Damage to the WMI repository or to security components can cause the same failure even when no other antivirus is installed.
commonCauses: A third-party antivirus suite has taken over protection and switched Defender off
An antivirus that was uninstalled left behind files, services or filter drivers
Damage to the WMI repository or to Security Center components
Defender platform files corrupted during an update

fixes.title: Find and completely remove any third-party antivirus
fixes.detail: In Settings > Apps, uninstall any non-Microsoft antivirus, since Windows normally does not let two run side by side. If parts of it remain, run the vendor's dedicated removal tool. Leftover filter drivers are the most common reason for 0x800106BA.

fixes.title: Check and restart the security services
fixes.detail: Open `services.msc` and make sure 'Microsoft Defender Antivirus Service' (called 'Windows Defender Antivirus Service' on older builds), 'Security Center' and 'Windows Defender Firewall' are not set to Disabled. Use the default Automatic or Manual startup type, then reboot. If any of them still refuses to start, write down the error it gives you for the later steps.

fixes.title: Run DISM and SFC to repair system files
fixes.detail: From an elevated Command Prompt, run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` and then `sfc /scannow`. This replaces damaged Defender platform files and the components they rely on.

fixes.title: Update the Defender definitions by hand
fixes.detail: Once the service is running, go to Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection updates > Check for updates. You can also run `MpCmdRun.exe -SignatureUpdate` from the Defender platform folder. If definition updates fail too, look into the Windows Update errors (for example `0x8024402f`).

prevention: Have only one active antivirus product on the PC
Use the vendor's cleanup tool whenever you uninstall a third-party antivirus
Let Defender platform updates finish before you shut down
Run `sfc /scannow` if Windows Security starts showing blank or unresponsive pages

title: "This app has been blocked for your protection"
codes: This app has been blocked for your protection
An administrator has blocked you from running this app
summary: SmartScreen or a UAC policy prevents an unsigned or flagged program or installer from running and shows 'This app has been blocked for your protection'. Usually the file still has its Zone.Identifier mark or comes from an untrusted publisher.
meaning: Nothing is broken here: this message comes from a security feature. Windows tags files downloaded from the internet with an NTFS Zone.Identifier mark, and it refuses to elevate binaries that are unsigned or signed with a revoked certificate. The block appears for truly dangerous files, and it also appears for older, legitimate installers.
commonCauses: The program was downloaded and still has the internet zone mark
The file is unsigned, or its publisher certificate has been revoked
A UAC Admin Approval policy that blocks every elevation request from standard users
Group Policy restrictions on a corporate PC, such as SmartScreen or managed installer rules

fixes.title: Unblock the file in Properties
fixes.detail: Right-click the installer and choose Properties. On the General tab, tick 'Unblock' (this box only shows up on downloaded files), then click Apply. That strips the zone mark, so do it only for files from a source you trust.
fixes.riskNote: Unblock a file only if you trust its publisher. Talking victims into this exact bypass is a standard malware trick.

fixes.title: Start the installer from an elevated Command Prompt
fixes.detail: Run Command Prompt as administrator and start the installer by typing its full path. If your account is an administrator but the policy is catching launches from File Explorer, running it in an elevated context gets past the UAC version of the block.

fixes.title: Check the publisher before you bypass anything
fixes.detail: Read the publisher name shown in the UAC prompt, then open the file's Properties > Digital Signatures tab. If the certificate is valid and matches the vendor on its official website, the block is a false positive. If it does not, delete the file.

fixes.title: Review SmartScreen and UAC policy settings
fixes.detail: If trusted software is blocked again and again, look at Windows Security > App & browser control > Reputation-based protection settings. On Pro editions, also open `gpedit.msc` and go to Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options, then review the 'User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode' group of policies. Put them back to their defaults instead of switching protection off.
fixes.riskNote: Turning down UAC or SmartScreen for the whole system weakens protection for every program. Unblocking individual files is the safer choice.

prevention: Get software only from the vendor's official website
Look at the digital signature before installing tools you do not recognize
Leave SmartScreen on and deal with each block individually

title: The Audio Service is Not Responding (no sound, red X on the speaker icon)
codes: The Audio Service is not responding
summary: You get the message 'The Audio Service is not responding' and a red X sits on the speaker icon in the taskbar. Either the Windows Audio service or the Windows Audio Endpoint Builder service has hung, or something they depend on has failed.
meaning: The audio troubleshooter reports this when it cannot start or communicate with `Audiosrv` (Windows Audio) or `AudioEndpointBuilder`. Common reasons include one of those services being set to Disabled, an audio driver that crashed while holding the endpoint, or a Windows update that swapped out parts of the audio stack while it was in use.
commonCauses: The Windows Audio or Windows Audio Endpoint Builder service is stopped or disabled
The audio driver crashed, or no longer matches after a Windows update
Audio enhancements or exclusive-mode conflicts locking up the playback endpoint
Third-party audio software, such as a DAW or virtual audio cable, holding on to the device

fixes.title: Restart both audio services
fixes.detail: Press Win+R and run `services.msc`. Restart 'Windows Audio Endpoint Builder' first, because restarting it also restarts the dependent service, then restart 'Windows Audio'. Set the Startup type of both to Automatic. In most cases nothing more is needed.

fixes.title: Run the Playing Audio troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters, find Playing Audio and click Run. It restarts the services, fixes the default device and checks the driver for you.

fixes.title: Reinstall the audio driver from Device Manager
fixes.detail: Open `devmgmt.msc`, expand Sound, video and game controllers, right-click your audio device and choose Uninstall device. Tick the option to delete the driver only if you plan to install the vendor's package afterwards. Then use Action > Scan for hardware changes, or run the vendor's driver installer, and reboot.
fixes.riskNote: Get drivers only from the PC or motherboard manufacturer's website so you do not install a package for the wrong model. If sound disappears completely after removal, fall back to the generic 'High Definition Audio Device' driver.

fixes.title: Turn off audio enhancements and exclusive mode
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Sound > More sound settings, select your playback device and click Properties. Switch off Enhancements and Spatial sound, and on the Advanced tab clear 'Allow applications to take exclusive control of this device'. With some drivers, conflicting enhancement chains make the service hang.

prevention: Install the audio driver from your PC maker before Windows Update replaces it with a generic one
Do not run two audio enhancement apps at once
Create a restore point before large graphics or audio driver updates

title: WSAPPX high CPU or disk usage (Store apps updating in the background)
summary: WSAPPX, the process that hosts the AppX Deployment Service and the Client License Service, keeps the CPU or disk busy for minutes on end. It is simply the Store installing and updating apps, but on slower PCs it can make everything sluggish.
meaning: WSAPPX is a legitimate Windows component, not malware, and you cannot simply turn it off because it installs and licenses every Microsoft Store app. When its usage stays high, a large app is usually being installed or updated, the Store is re-registering packages, or deployment is caught in a loop retrying the same failed package.
commonCauses: Large Store apps downloading or updating in the background
AppX deployment repeatedly retrying a corrupt package
Automatic Store updates starting while you are gaming or working
Lots of apps being provisioned at once, for example on a new PC or a fresh OEM image

fixes.title: Let the updates finish, or pause them
fixes.detail: Open the Microsoft Store, go to Library and click Get updates, then let everything pending complete; disk and network activity should calm down afterwards. If you prefer to update on your own schedule, click your profile icon in the Store, open Settings and turn off 'App updates', then update manually.

fixes.title: Clear the Store cache with WSReset
fixes.detail: Press Win+R and run `wsreset.exe`. When deployment is stuck retrying a broken package, resetting the cache breaks the loop, and WSAPPX settles down once the Store reopens.

fixes.title: Repair, reset or remove the heavy app
fixes.detail: The App history tab in Task Manager shows how much CPU time each Store app has used. For the worst offender, open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, choose the app's Advanced options and use Repair or Reset. Uninstall any apps you no longer need.

fixes.title: Run the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter, then DISM
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters and run Windows Store Apps. If deployment errors continue, run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` in an elevated Command Prompt to repair the servicing stack.

prevention: Run Store updates yourself at a time that suits you
Remove Store apps you do not use
Keep a healthy amount of free space on the system drive

title: SVCHOST high memory usage (Service Host using too much RAM)
summary: In Task Manager, one or more 'Service Host' (svchost.exe) processes are using gigabytes of memory. Svchost is only a container for Windows services, so the real job is finding out which service inside it is growing.
meaning: Svchost.exe runs groups of Windows services such as networking, Windows Update, telemetry and audio. When memory climbs, the usual owners are Windows Update with a bloated download cache, the Windows Event Log, SysMain (formerly Superfetch), or malware pretending to be a service host. Windows 10 and 11 split most services into their own host processes, so Task Manager can show you which service is responsible.
commonCauses: The Windows Update service stuck with an oversized download cache in SoftwareDistribution
SysMain (Superfetch) prefetching heavily on hard-disk systems
A memory leak in a third-party service running inside a host process
Malware posing as svchost and running from a folder outside the system directories

fixes.title: Find out which service is using the memory
fixes.detail: In Task Manager, open the Details tab, locate the svchost.exe entry with the high memory figure, right-click it and select 'Go to service(s)'. The services that get highlighted are the ones responsible. Write their names down before you change anything.

fixes.title: Empty the Windows Update download cache
fixes.detail: If the culprit is wuauserv or BITS, open an elevated Command Prompt and run `net stop wuauserv` and `net stop bits`. Rename `C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution` to `SoftwareDistribution.old`, then run `net start bits` and `net start wuauserv`. Windows Update recreates the folder and downloads cleanly into it.
fixes.riskNote: Stopping the update services in the middle of an install can make queued updates download again. Skip this while a feature update is visibly installing.

fixes.title: Run a full scan with Microsoft Defender
fixes.detail: Go to Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options, choose Full scan and start it. The real svchost.exe lives only in C:\Windows\System32 (and C:\Windows\SysWOW64). Use 'Open file location' in Task Manager to check, and treat a copy anywhere else as suspicious.

fixes.title: Adjust SysMain and look for driver memory leaks
fixes.detail: On PCs with only hard disks, stopping SysMain in `services.msc` can free a steady chunk of memory. If usage grows after sleep or a driver update, look for a pattern in Reliability Monitor and update the driver involved. Testing RAM with `mdsched.exe` rules out faulty memory that only looks like a leak.
fixes.riskNote: Turning services off just to save RAM can break features that run in the background. SysMain can be stopped and restarted safely, but research any other service before you stop it.

prevention: Restart the PC now and then so services that leak memory are reloaded
Keep Windows Update healthy, since a stuck cache is the most common cause
Install drivers from reputable vendors and check Reliability Monitor after updates

title: BOOTMGR is missing (Press Ctrl+Alt+Del to restart)
codes: BOOTMGR is missing. Press Ctrl+Alt+Del to restart
summary: The PC's firmware cannot locate the Windows Boot Manager file (BOOTMGR), so startup stops with 'BOOTMGR is missing. Press Ctrl+Alt+Del to restart' before Windows has a chance to load.
meaning: BOOTMGR is the first piece of Windows that the firmware runs. When the firmware checks the wrong disk, or when the file on the system or EFI partition is missing, unreadable or compressed, startup stops at this message, and pressing Ctrl+Alt+Del only brings you back to it. This is a different problem from a missing BCD store or a missing winload.efi: in this case, the very first stage of the Windows boot chain cannot be found.
commonCauses: The BIOS/UEFI boot order points at the wrong disk, or a USB drive that is not bootable is still plugged in
BOOTMGR is missing or damaged on the EFI or System Reserved partition after a failed update, a power cut or disk cloning
The system drive has been compressed, which triggers the 'BOOTMGR is compressed' version of the message
The boot mode (UEFI versus Legacy/CSM) changed after the firmware settings were reset
A disk with file-system errors or failing sectors that can no longer read the boot files

fixes.title: Unplug USB drives and check the boot order
fixes.detail: Disconnect all USB sticks and external drives and restart. If the error is still there, open the firmware setup (usually F2, Del or Esc on the logo screen) and check two things: that the Windows disk appears at all, and that it is first in the boot order.

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair in the recovery environment
fixes.detail: Get into Windows Recovery, either by interrupting startup three times in a row or by holding Shift while you click Restart. Choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair and let it finish. It is built for exactly this kind of boot-file damage and is the least invasive fix.

fixes.title: Fix the boot records with bootrec
fixes.detail: In WinRE, go to Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Command Prompt and run these in order: `bootrec /fixmbr`, `bootrec /fixboot`, `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. When asked whether to add your Windows installation to the boot list, type Y, then restart.
fixes.riskNote: `/fixmbr` and `/fixboot` overwrite the MBR and boot sector. They are usually harmless on UEFI/GPT systems, but make sure the prompt is working on the disk you mean to repair and never on another one.

fixes.title: Rebuild the boot files with bcdboot
fixes.detail: If bootrec did not solve it, open Command Prompt in WinRE and run `diskpart`, then `list vol` to identify the EFI volume. Run `select vol <n>`, `assign letter=S` and `exit`. Then run `bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI`, which recreates the boot files and BCD store on the EFI partition. On older BIOS/MBR systems, `bcdboot C:\Windows` is enough.
fixes.riskNote: Check carefully which volume gets the drive letter in diskpart, because boot files written to the wrong partition will leave the disk unable to boot. Inside WinRE the Windows partition may not be C:, so confirm the letter first.

fixes.title: Decompress the boot manager (BOOTMGR is compressed)
fixes.detail: When the message reads 'BOOTMGR is compressed', the entire system drive was compressed, for example with the 'Compress this drive' option. Open Command Prompt in WinRE, run `compact /u C:\bootmgr` and restart. Once Windows is running, open the properties of C: and clear 'Compress this drive to save disk space'.
fixes.riskNote: Never compress the Windows system drive. Compressing it hides boot files and causes exactly this failure. Use Disk Cleanup if you need free space.

fixes.title: Check the disk
fixes.detail: If it still fails, the disk itself may have errors or be failing. In WinRE's Command Prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f /r` and look for reports of unreadable sectors. If the problem keeps coming back after a boot repair succeeds, the drive is probably failing, so back up your data before doing anything else.

prevention: Do not compress the Windows system drive
Keep the Windows disk at the top of the firmware boot order and unplug bootable USB sticks when you are done with them
When cloning, use a tool that copies the EFI or System Reserved partition as well as C:
Shut down properly, because losing power during an update is a classic cause of damaged boot files

title: Operating System Not Found (no bootable device detected)
summary: The firmware completes its startup checks but cannot find any device with a bootable operating system. You see 'Operating System Not Found' or 'An operating system wasn't found. Try disconnecting any drives that don't contain an operating system.'
meaning: This goes a step further than a BOOTMGR error: the firmware never finds a boot loader to hand control to. The disk may have vanished from the controller's list, the boot order may point at another device, or the storage controller mode may have changed so the disk's boot data is unusable. It often shows up after the BIOS/UEFI settings reset themselves (a flat CMOS battery), after a BIOS update, or when a cable or drive fails. A disk that is detected only some of the time is frequently a disk that is about to die.
commonCauses: A wrong or reset boot order, for example a dead CMOS battery wiping BIOS settings at every power-off
The SATA controller mode no longer matches (AHCI versus IDE or RAID) after a firmware reset, so the installed OS cannot be seen
The disk is not detected at all because of a loose SATA or NVMe connection, a loose power cable, or a dead drive
A failing disk with unreadable sectors in the area that holds the boot files
A damaged MBR or EFI system partition after cloning or a power event

fixes.title: See what the firmware detects
fixes.detail: Open the BIOS/UEFI setup (F2 or Del on the logo screen) and review both the boot order and the list of drives. If the Windows disk does not appear anywhere, go straight to the hardware steps below, because no software fix can help until the firmware sees the drive.

fixes.title: Reseat the drive and its cables
fixes.detail: Shut down, unplug the power, and reseat the SATA data and power cables, or reseat the M.2/NVMe module in a laptop. A connector that is only partly seated produces this exact symptom. While testing, leave only the Windows drive connected and unplug any USB drives.
fixes.riskNote: Discharge static by touching grounded metal before handling internal parts, and never force an M.2 connector.

fixes.title: Set the SATA controller mode back
fixes.detail: In BIOS/UEFI, find the SATA or storage mode setting (AHCI, IDE, or RAID/Intel RST) and return it to the mode Windows was installed in. A firmware reset that switches AHCI to IDE or RAID can hide the boot disk, and changing the mode without preparation later leads to INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE.
fixes.riskNote: Do not try modes at random. Starting Windows in a different controller mode from the one it was installed with can cause a boot-device blue screen that requires repairs from recovery.

fixes.title: Replace the CMOS battery if settings keep resetting
fixes.detail: When the BIOS forgets the clock and the boot order every time the PC is switched off, the coin-cell battery on the motherboard has run out. Fit a new one (a CR2032 in most desktops) and set the boot order correctly again.

fixes.title: Repair the disk using recovery media
fixes.detail: If the firmware sees the drive but Windows still will not load, boot from Windows installation media, choose 'Repair your computer' and open Command Prompt. Run `chkdsk C: /f /r` to fix file-system damage that may be hiding the boot files, then check the boot entries with `bootrec /rebuildbcd`.

fixes.title: Check the drive's health and back up right away
fixes.detail: A disk that keeps disappearing is usually failing. When you can get into Windows, or by connecting the drive to another PC with a USB adapter, check its SMART status: in Command Prompt, `wmic diskdrive get status` should return OK. Back up your files before attempting any more repairs, and replace the drive if the errors continue.
fixes.riskNote: Each extra boot attempt on a failing disk raises the risk of losing data for good, so back up before you run repair tools.

prevention: Replace the CMOS battery as soon as the BIOS starts losing its settings
Keep a Windows installation USB drive ready, which turns this dead end into a fixable problem
When cloning a disk, always include the EFI or System Reserved partition
Back up regularly, because a disk that is detected only sometimes is warning you it may fail

title: Stuck on 'Preparing Automatic Repair' (endless repair loop)
codes: Automatic Repair couldn't repair your PC
summary: Each time it starts, Windows goes to 'Preparing Automatic Repair' or 'Diagnosing your PC', then either keeps looping or finishes with 'Automatic Repair couldn't repair your PC'. The desktop never appears.
meaning: When two boot attempts fail in a row, Windows opens its recovery environment and runs Startup Repair on its own. A loop tells you something in the boot path really is broken: Startup Repair runs, cannot fix it, and Windows tries to start again. Startup Repair writes a log to `C:\Windows\System32\Logfiles\Srt\SrtTrail.txt`, and that file often identifies the real cause, such as disk errors, missing or corrupt system files, or a faulty driver or update.
commonCauses: System or boot files corrupted by an interrupted update or a power cut
Disk errors or a failing drive that leave system files unreadable
Corrupted BCD (Boot Configuration Data)
A Windows update or driver installed recently that prevents startup
Faulty hardware, most often a failing disk or bad RAM

fixes.title: Reach the recovery menu on purpose
fixes.detail: If the screen sits on 'Preparing Automatic Repair', turn the PC off while the loading dots are spinning, three times in a row. Windows then shows the 'Automatic Repair' screen with an 'Advanced options' button. Go to Troubleshoot > Advanced options. Unplug USB devices first, since a misbehaving peripheral can be what starts the loop.
fixes.riskNote: Hold the power button only while the spinner is on screen. Cutting power repeatedly at other points can make file corruption worse.

fixes.title: Start with System Restore
fixes.detail: Under Troubleshoot > Advanced options > System Restore, choose a restore point from before the loop started, which is often just before a Windows update or a new driver. It reverts system files and drivers but leaves your personal files alone.
fixes.riskNote: Any apps, drivers and updates installed after the restore point will be removed. Documents and photos are not affected.

fixes.title: Boot into Safe Mode and turn off automatic restart
fixes.detail: Go to Advanced options > Startup Settings > Restart and press 4 to start in Safe Mode. If that works, uninstall the latest update (Settings > Windows Update > Update history > Uninstall updates) or the newest driver in Device Manager. In Startup Settings you can also pick 'Disable automatic restart after failure', so any stop code stays on screen and the PC does not just reboot.

fixes.title: Run chkdsk and offline SFC from WinRE
fixes.detail: Open Advanced options > Command Prompt and run `chkdsk C: /f /r`. The Windows drive letter can be different in WinRE, so confirm it first with `dir C:`. Then run `sfc /scannow /offbootdir=C:\ /offwindir=C:\Windows`. These repair file-system damage and system-file corruption that Startup Repair could not handle.

fixes.title: Rebuild the BCD using bootrec
fixes.detail: From the same Command Prompt, run `bootrec /fixmbr`, `bootrec /fixboot` and `bootrec /rebuildbcd`, answering Y when asked to add the installation it finds. This goes straight at the problem when SrtTrail.txt or the history of the loop points to corrupted boot configuration.

fixes.title: Reset this PC and keep your files
fixes.detail: When nothing else works, choose Troubleshoot > Reset this PC > 'Keep my files'. Windows is reinstalled and your personal data is kept. If you can reach the disk from Safe Mode or a live USB, copy anything irreplaceable somewhere safe first.
fixes.riskNote: Even with 'Keep my files', installed programs are removed. Pick 'Remove everything' only once your data is backed up.

prevention: Leave Windows Update on and let updates finish, since interrupting them invites boot corruption
Keep at least 15% of the system drive free so repair steps have room to work
Create a restore point before installing driver or feature updates
Take slow startups and disk warnings seriously, because a failing drive is a frequent trigger

title: ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED
summary: Chrome or Edge reports ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED with 'This site can't be reached' when the destination actively turns down the connection. Most often nothing is listening on that port, or something on your PC is blocking it.
meaning: Your browser got as far as the destination, but the TCP connection was rejected instead of accepted. The server's service may be down or listening on another port, a firewall or security suite may be blocking you, or a leftover proxy setting on your PC may point to a local service that no longer exists. With 'localhost refused to connect', the development or test server on your own machine simply is not running on the port you typed.
commonCauses: The website's server is down, overloaded, or now uses a different port
A firewall or antivirus program blocking connections from the browser
Old proxy settings that point at a local proxy which has since been removed
A damaged Winsock or network stack after malware removal or uninstalling software
For localhost, the dev server is not running or you opened the wrong port

fixes.title: Reload, then narrow down where the problem is
fixes.detail: Press Ctrl+F5 for a hard reload. Next, try the site in a different browser and on a different device or over mobile data. If nothing can connect, the website's server is down, so wait or contact the site owner. If only your PC fails, carry on with the steps below.

fixes.title: Clear the DNS cache
fixes.detail: In Command Prompt, run `ipconfig /flushdns` and reload the page. This throws away stale lookups that could be sending you to a server address that no longer accepts connections.

fixes.title: Switch off proxy settings
fixes.detail: In Settings > Network & Internet > Proxy, turn off 'Automatically detect settings' and remove any 'Use a proxy server' configuration, then reload. To also clear the system-wide WinHTTP proxy that services use, run `netsh winhttp reset proxy` in an elevated Command Prompt.
fixes.riskNote: Work PCs sometimes require a proxy. Put the setting back if your managed network depends on it.

fixes.title: Test whether a firewall or antivirus is blocking you
fixes.detail: Briefly turn off the web, HTTPS or 'web shield' protection in your third-party antivirus or firewall and reload. If the site now opens, switch protection back on and allow your browser through it, for example in Windows Security > Firewall & network protection > 'Allow an app through firewall'.
fixes.riskNote: Keep security software off only for the quick test and turn it back on straight away.

fixes.title: Reset the Winsock catalog
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` in an elevated Command Prompt and restart the computer. This rebuilds the network provider stack if it was damaged when security or VPN software was uninstalled.
fixes.riskNote: After a Winsock reset, some VPN or LSP-based software and custom filtering settings may need to be set up again.

fixes.title: For localhost, check the server and the port
fixes.detail: If only local addresses are refused, your local server is not running on that port. Start it, then check that it is listening with `netstat -ano | findstr :3000`, replacing 3000 with your port. Use exactly the same port in the address bar, for example http://localhost:3000.

prevention: Clear out leftover proxy settings after removing VPN or filtering software
Run only one security suite with web protection turned on
Bookmark your dev server URLs including the correct port
After installing and removing a lot of network software, consider running `netsh winsock reset`

title: ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT
summary: Chrome or Edge shows ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT along with 'This site can't be reached' and '<site> took too long to respond'. The server never replied to the connection attempt, which means packets are getting lost somewhere between your PC and the site.
meaning: A refusal is an answer; a timeout is silence. The browser asked to connect and got no reply before it gave up. The packets are typically dropped by a router that has stalled, a firewall that discards traffic instead of rejecting it, a DNS answer that points to an unreachable address, a weak wireless connection, or a destination server that is overloaded or down. The most useful first question is whether every site times out or just one.
commonCauses: A router or modem that has hung and is dropping new connections
DNS returning an address for a server that is dead or unreachable
A firewall, VPN or antivirus quietly filtering the connection
The destination server being overloaded or offline, especially busy sites at peak times
Occasionally, an MTU mismatch on VPN or PPPoE links that silently drops large packets

fixes.title: Try other sites and other devices
fixes.detail: Open a few different websites. If they all time out, the problem is on your side (router or PC). If only one site times out, and it does so on every device, that site is down or blocking you, so try again later.

fixes.title: Restart the router and modem
fixes.detail: Unplug the router and the modem or ONT for 30 seconds. Plug the modem in first, then the router, and wait until the connection is fully back. This clears jammed connection tables and is the most effective fix when every site times out.

fixes.title: Use a dependable public DNS server
fixes.detail: Go to Settings > Network & Internet, select your adapter, then next to DNS server assignment click Edit and choose Manual. Enter 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare) or 8.8.8.8 (Google) as the preferred DNS. Alternatively, run `netsh interface ip set dns name="Ethernet" static 1.1.1.1` in an elevated Command Prompt, replacing Ethernet with your adapter's name. Afterwards run `ipconfig /flushdns` and reload.
fixes.riskNote: On managed or corporate networks, you may need the company or ISP DNS servers to reach internal names.

fixes.title: Get a fresh IP address
fixes.detail: Run `ipconfig /release` and then `ipconfig /renew` in Command Prompt, or just turn Wi-Fi off and back on, to obtain a new lease. Follow up with `ipconfig /flushdns` and reload the page.

fixes.title: Take VPN, proxy and security filters out of the path
fixes.detail: Disconnect from any VPN, turn off the proxy under Settings > Network & Internet > Proxy, and pause your antivirus web filtering, then reload. If the site opens, turn the layers back on one by one to see which one is dropping the traffic.

fixes.title: Reset the network stack
fixes.detail: Open an elevated Command Prompt, run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset`, then restart. This wipes corrupted Winsock and TCP/IP settings left by removed software or driver problems.
fixes.riskNote: You may have to set up static IP addresses and some VPN clients again afterwards.

prevention: If your ISP's router is known to hang, restart it on a regular schedule
Use fast anycast public DNS resolvers such as 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8
Keep network adapter drivers up to date from the manufacturer
Use a wired connection or strong 5 GHz Wi-Fi for long downloads

title: ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR
codes: This site can't provide a secure connection
summary: Chrome or Edge shows ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR with the message 'This site can't provide a secure connection'. The HTTPS (TLS) handshake broke down before a secure connection could be set up.
meaning: The browser made contact, but the TLS negotiation failed. Possible reasons include a certificate that cannot be validated (frequently because the PC's clock is wrong), a security product that intercepts HTTPS and re-signs it with a certificate Windows does not trust, disabled TLS versions or stale SSL state, or a misconfigured server. Anything that sits between you and the website and re-encrypts traffic, such as antivirus HTTPS scanning, filtering proxies or certain VPNs, should be high on your suspect list.
commonCauses: A wrong system date or time that makes certificates look invalid
HTTPS (SSL) scanning in an antivirus or firewall intercepting the connection
A stale SSL cache, or TLS 1.2 and 1.3 turned off in the protocol settings
Damaged Winsock settings after security software was changed or removed
A TLS problem on the server, such as an outdated setup or a broken certificate

fixes.title: Check the date, time and time zone
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Time & language > Date & time, turn on 'Set time automatically' and 'Set time zone automatically', and click 'Sync now'. Certificates are valid only within exact dates, so a clock that has drifted is the most common reason for this error. You can also force a sync with `w32tm /resync` in an elevated Command Prompt.

fixes.title: Clear the SSL state
fixes.detail: Press Win+R, enter `inetcpl.cpl` and press Enter. On the Content tab, click 'Clear SSL state'. This removes cached certificate and SSL session data that can get stuck after a site changes its certificate.

fixes.title: Check the TLS protocol settings
fixes.detail: In the same `inetcpl.cpl` window, open the Advanced tab and scroll down to the Security section. Make sure 'Use TLS 1.2' is ticked, along with 'Use TLS 1.3' if it is listed, and that the outdated SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 options stay off. Browsers and websites refuse handshakes over retired protocols.
fixes.riskNote: Do not turn on legacy SSL 3.0 or TLS 1.0 hoping to fix this. They are insecure, and modern servers reject them anyway.

fixes.title: Briefly turn off antivirus HTTPS scanning
fixes.detail: Many security suites, along with some parental control and web filter tools, intercept HTTPS traffic. Switch off the feature (often called 'HTTPS scanning' or 'Scan encrypted connections') for a moment and reload. If the site works, add your browser to the product's exclusion or trusted list instead of leaving the feature disabled.
fixes.riskNote: Turn the protection back on as soon as you finish testing, and do not browse with it off.

fixes.title: Reset the Winsock catalog
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` in an elevated Command Prompt and restart. Layered service providers left over from security or VPN software often break TLS handshakes.
fixes.riskNote: You may need to set up VPN clients and network filters again after the reset.

fixes.title: Rule out a network that intercepts traffic
fixes.detail: Load the site on a different network, such as a phone hotspot, and in another browser. If it works there, the hotel, office or firewall network you were on is intercepting TLS, so switch networks or ask its administrator. Also look in Settings > Network & Internet > Proxy for a filtering proxy.

prevention: Leave 'Set time automatically' on so the clock always agrees with certificates
Choose security suites that use the Windows certificate store for HTTPS scanning
Never fall back to legacy SSL or TLS versions
Clean up after uninstalling VPN or filter software, and run a Winsock reset afterwards

title: Microsoft Store error 0x80073CF3: app install blocked by a package conflict
codes: package failed updates, dependency or conflict validation
summary: You try to install or update a Store app and get 0x80073CF3. Windows ran its pre-install checks on the AppX package and stopped because it clashes with something already on the machine, such as a second version of the app, a dependency that is missing, or an update that never finished.
meaning: Microsoft documents 0x80073CF3 as "package failed updates, dependency or conflict validation." Before any Store package is installed, the deployment service compares it with the apps already present and with the pending update queue. This error means the package did not pass that comparison. In practice, the usual culprits are a duplicate or older copy of the same app that was installed outside the Store, a framework or runtime package the app depends on that is absent or the wrong version, or an earlier update that was only partly applied.
commonCauses: The same app is already present in another version, either sideloaded or an older Store release
A framework or runtime package the app needs is missing or incompatible
An update for this package is stuck in the deployment queue
The Store cache is corrupted and misreports what is installed
AppX deployment components in the Windows image are damaged

fixes.title: Clear the Store cache with WSReset
fixes.detail: Open the Run box with Win+R, enter `wsreset.exe`, and let it finish. The Store reopens on its own with an empty cache. Try the install again: leftover staging data is a frequent reason validation fails.

fixes.title: Finish any updates that are already queued
fixes.detail: In the Store, go to Library and click 'Get updates'. Then open Settings → Windows Update and choose 'Check for updates'. Very often the conflict is a waiting update for the same app or one of its frameworks, and once it completes your install can go ahead.

fixes.title: Uninstall the duplicate version of the app
fixes.detail: Go to Settings → Apps → Installed apps and look for the app plus any older, duplicate or sideloaded copy. Remove them, restart the PC, and install a fresh copy from the Store. With only one version on the system, the conflict check has nothing to trip over.

fixes.title: Register the Microsoft Store again
fixes.detail: Start PowerShell with administrator rights and paste: `Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers Microsoft.WindowsStore | Foreach {Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register "$($_.InstallLocation)\AppXManifest.xml"}`. This re-creates the Store's own registration so it can stage new packages properly.
fixes.riskNote: Close the Store before running it and paste the command exactly as shown. Pointing the registration at the wrong package path can create new AppX errors.

fixes.title: Repair the Windows image with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: From a Command Prompt opened as administrator, run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` and, when it completes, `sfc /scannow`. If the system image itself is damaged, this restores the components responsible for validating and registering Store packages.

prevention: Stick to one install source per app on each PC; mixing sideloaded and Store copies invites conflicts
Wait for running Store updates to complete before starting new installs
Reach for WSReset as soon as Store installs begin failing for no clear reason
Leave Windows Update on so shared frameworks stay at compatible versions

title: Microsoft Store error 0x80073D02: package files are in use
codes: package could not be installed because resources it modifies are currently in use
summary: An app will not install, update or uninstall from the Store, and you see 0x80073D02 (ERROR_PACKAGES_IN_USE). Some running app still has that package's files or resources open, so Windows cannot change them.
meaning: Windows will not replace an AppX package while a process is using it. Microsoft's description of 0x80073D02 is "package could not be installed because resources it modifies are currently in use." Usually the app you are updating is still running, possibly only in the background, or another app or shared framework it hosts has a lock on the files. The error is harmless in itself and disappears once those locks are let go.
commonCauses: The app you are updating or removing is still open, or suspended in the background
Another app built on the same framework or runtime has the package open
A Store or AppX background process is holding an outdated lock
An update is waiting on a restart that has not happened yet

fixes.title: Fully close the app and try again
fixes.detail: Shut every window of the app. Then press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager and end any leftover background process for that app, along with Microsoft Store. Retry the install or update right away.

fixes.title: Reboot the computer
fixes.detail: Restarting frees all package locks and lets any updates that were waiting on a reboot finish, and that pending work is frequently the very operation that failed. Once Windows is back, open the Store, go to Library and click Get updates.

fixes.title: Run WSReset to clear the Store cache
fixes.detail: Press Win+R, enter `wsreset.exe`, and wait for the Store to reopen before retrying. This wipes stale handles and staging data the Store keeps for itself.

fixes.title: Register the Microsoft Store again
fixes.detail: If the Store keeps locking files, open PowerShell as administrator and run `Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers Microsoft.WindowsStore | Foreach {Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register "$($_.InstallLocation)\AppXManifest.xml"}` to rebuild its registration.
fixes.riskNote: Close every Store window beforehand and paste the command without changes.

fixes.title: Install outstanding Windows updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings → Windows Update, click 'Check for updates', install whatever is offered, and restart when prompted. Servicing tasks that are still pending often tie up the same resources the Store is trying to use.

prevention: On machines that rarely sit idle, close apps before kicking off Store updates
Restart when Windows asks; queued app updates keep their locks until you do
Let Library updates in the Store run to completion instead of canceling them partway

title: 0x80070035: The network path was not found
codes: The network path was not found
summary: When you open a shared folder or NAS, Windows reports that it cannot access \\server\share and shows error code 0x80070035, "The network path was not found." In short, the SMB path you entered cannot be resolved or reached from this PC.
meaning: 0x80070035 maps to ERROR_BAD_NETPATH. The SMB client tried to translate \\server\share into a host it could talk to and failed. That can happen because the name did not resolve, the target machine is off or sleeping, discovery services are turned off so the path is wrong, or a firewall is dropping SMB traffic. Current Windows versions add one more possibility: SMB1 is off by default for security reasons, so very old NAS boxes and routers that only understand SMB1 simply cannot be found.
commonCauses: Network discovery or the Function Discovery services are turned off, so the device name never resolves
The target PC or NAS is powered off, asleep, or its name cannot be resolved (test with the IP address)
The firewall blocks File and Printer Sharing, or the network is set to the Public profile
An outdated cached share mapping or saved credential left over from a server change
An older device that only supports SMB1, which is disabled out of the box on Windows 10 and 11

fixes.title: Confirm you can reach the target
fixes.detail: In Command Prompt, run `ping ServerName`. If that fails, try `ping 192.168.x.x` using the device's IP address. When the IP replies but the name does not, you have a name resolution problem: connect with `\\192.168.x.x\share` or repair discovery using the steps below. If the IP does not answer either, the device is off, asleep, or not properly connected.

fixes.title: Turn on network discovery and file sharing
fixes.detail: Go to Settings → Network & Internet → Advanced network settings → Advanced sharing settings. For the active profile, switch on 'Network discovery' and 'File and printer sharing', and make sure the network is set to Private, because the Public profile blocks sharing on purpose. Apply these settings on both computers.

fixes.title: Get the Function Discovery services running
fixes.detail: From an elevated Command Prompt, run `net start FDResPub`, `net start fdPHost`, `net start SSDPSRV` and `net start upnphost`. Alternatively, open services.msc and set 'Function Discovery Resource Publication', 'Function Discovery Provider Host', 'SSDP Discovery' and 'UPnP Device Host' to Automatic. When these are stopped, PCs no longer advertise themselves on the network.

fixes.title: Map the share directly to test it
fixes.detail: Type `net use` to see current connections and clear the outdated one with `net use \\Server\Share /delete`. Next, create a new mapping with `net use Z: \\Server\Share /persistent:no` and supply credentials when asked. A fresh mapping sidesteps cached Explorer state and proves whether the path works.
fixes.riskNote: Running `net use * /delete /y` removes every mapped drive on the computer in one go, so delete just the entry you need instead.

fixes.title: Let File and Printer Sharing through the firewall
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security → Firewall & network protection → 'Allow an app through firewall' and tick 'File and Printer Sharing' for Private networks. To enable the full rule group from an elevated Command Prompt, use `netsh advfirewall firewall set rule group="File and Printer Sharing" new enable=Yes`. Also check that the target accepts SMB on port 445 by running `Test-NetConnection ServerName -Port 445` in PowerShell.
fixes.riskNote: The rule group name is translated on non-English editions of Windows, so use the checkbox in the GUI rather than the netsh command on those systems.

fixes.title: Last resort for very old devices: SMB1
fixes.detail: If the target is an aging NAS or router whose shares used to work years ago, it may support nothing newer than the retired SMB 1.0 protocol. Your first options should be a firmware update or switching to the device's web interface or FTP. Only on a home network you trust, open 'Turn Windows features on or off', enable 'SMB 1.0/CIFS Client', and restart.
fixes.riskNote: SMB1 is outdated and widely abused by malware to spread. Turn it on only temporarily, never on business or untrusted networks, and switch it off again once the device has been replaced or migrated.

prevention: On home networks, leave network discovery and the Function Discovery services switched on
Assign NAS devices a static IP or a DHCP reservation and connect by IP when you can
Mark home Wi-Fi and Ethernet connections as Private rather than Public
Update the firmware on, or retire, any device that still depends on SMB1

title: 0x8007052E: ERROR_LOGON_FAILURE (The user name or password is incorrect)
codes: The user name or password is incorrect
summary: A mapped drive, scheduled task, Windows service or remote connection fails with 0x8007052E, ERROR_LOGON_FAILURE, and the message "The user name or password is incorrect." Put simply, the target does not accept the credentials Windows is sending.
meaning: 0x8007052E is an authentication failure: the remote side turned down the username and password Windows supplied. It most often shows up right after a password change, since Windows quietly keeps reusing old saved credentials stored in Credential Manager, in a mapped drive, in a scheduled task, or in the 'Log on as' settings of a service. Fixing it nearly always comes down to updating the credential in the specific place that is still holding the old one.
commonCauses: Credential Manager still holds the old password after it was changed
A mapped drive is reconnecting with a saved, outdated password
A scheduled task or Windows service runs under an account whose stored password is out of date
The username is in the wrong format: DOMAIN\user vs user@domain vs .\localuser
The account on the target is disabled, expired, or locked out after too many failed attempts

fixes.title: Type the credentials in the format the target expects
fixes.detail: At the sign-in prompt, enter the username the way the target wants it. Domain accounts use `DOMAIN\username`, Azure AD (Entra) style sign-ins use the UPN `user@domain.com`, and local accounts on the target use `ComputerName\username` or `.\username`. Getting the format wrong is enough on its own to trigger this error.

fixes.title: Remove the outdated drive mapping and map it again
fixes.detail: Open Command Prompt, run `net use` to see your mappings, and delete the old one with `net use \\Server\Share /delete`. Then remap it with `net use Z: \\Server\Share /user:DOMAIN\username` and type the new password when Windows asks.
fixes.riskNote: `net use * /delete /y` drops all mapped drives at once, so if other mappings are in use, remove only the broken one.

fixes.title: Clean up Credential Manager
fixes.detail: Open Control Panel → Credential Manager (or run `control keymgr.dll`), go to Windows Credentials, and edit or remove the entry for the server. From the command line, `cmdkey /list` shows saved entries, `cmdkey /delete:ServerName` removes one, and `cmdkey /add:ServerName /user:DOMAIN\username` adds it back (you get a secure prompt, or you can add `/pass:` in scripts). Reconnect afterward.
fixes.riskNote: Keep passwords out of scripts and command history where possible; the interactive prompt from `net use` or Credential Manager is safer.

fixes.title: Update the password on tasks and services
fixes.detail: In Task Scheduler, open the task's Properties, go to Security options, click 'Change User or Group' and enter the password again. In services.msc, open the service's Properties, switch to the Log On tab, re-enter the password, and restart the service. Both keep their own stored copy of the password, so they need updating every time the account password changes.

fixes.title: Confirm the account is healthy on the target
fixes.detail: On the target machine, or with help from its administrator, check that the account exists, is enabled, has not been locked out by failed sign-ins, and does not have an expired password. For domain accounts, try signing in on the target directly: that tells you whether the issue is the account itself or cached credentials on your own PC.

prevention: Whenever a password changes, refresh it in Credential Manager, mapped drives, scheduled tasks and services that use that account
Run scheduled tasks and services under a dedicated service account with a written password-change procedure
Always connect to a server by the same name so its credentials live in a single entry
If an account gets locked out, unlock it first before chasing other causes

title: IDT High Definition Audio CODEC error 10 (This device cannot start)
codes: IDT High Definition Audio CODEC error 10
IDT High Definition Audio CODEC Code 10
summary: Sound disappears entirely and Device Manager lists the IDT High Definition Audio CODEC with "This device cannot start. (Code 10)." This typically happens when Windows Update or a version upgrade swaps the manufacturer's IDT driver for a generic or faulty one.
meaning: Many HP, Sony and Dell laptops use IDT audio chips, and the drivers for them are tailored by each manufacturer. Following a Windows upgrade or a driver 'update', the built-in High Definition Audio driver may fail to initialize the IDT codec, so the device's start routine fails with Code 10 and no playback or recording devices remain. The chip itself is seldom defective. In nearly every case the problem is the driver state, which is why rebooting does not clear it.
commonCauses: Windows Update replaced the manufacturer's IDT driver with a generic or wrong one
The IDT driver's state was corrupted during a Windows version upgrade, the textbook post-upgrade Code 10
A power-management glitch left the codec stuck after sleep or Fast Startup (hybrid shutdown)
The codec hardware has actually failed (uncommon)

fixes.title: Do a full shutdown and drain residual power
fixes.detail: Choose Shut down rather than Restart, disconnect the charger, press and hold the power button for roughly 30 seconds, then turn the laptop on. This resets a stuck power state in the codec that an ordinary restart leaves alone, and it resolves a surprising number of Code 10 audio problems.

fixes.title: Remove the device and let Windows detect it again
fixes.detail: Open `devmgmt.msc`, expand Sound, video and game controllers, right-click 'IDT High Definition Audio CODEC' and pick Uninstall device (leave the driver in place if you are not sure). Then use Action → Scan for hardware changes, and Windows sets the device up from scratch.

fixes.title: Roll the driver back
fixes.detail: If sound stopped right after a Windows or driver update, open the device's Properties, go to the Driver tab and click 'Roll Back Driver'. The earlier IDT driver is normally still stored on the disk.

fixes.title: Get the IDT driver from your laptop manufacturer
fixes.detail: On the HP, Sony or Dell support site, download the IDT (or Beats) audio package for your exact model, run the installer and restart. Manufacturer packages include the codec-specific settings that the generic driver does not have.
fixes.riskNote: Download only from the PC or motherboard maker's site. Installing an audio package meant for a different model is a common way to make a driver problem worse.

fixes.title: Switch to the generic High Definition Audio Device driver
fixes.detail: In Device Manager choose Update driver → 'Browse my computer for drivers' → 'Let me pick from a list of available drivers', select 'High Definition Audio Device' and click Next. When the IDT driver cannot be repaired, Microsoft's generic class driver frequently brings back basic sound.
fixes.riskNote: You get working audio but lose manufacturer extras such as the equalizer app and jack-detection pop-ups. Move back to the OEM package once a correct version is available.

prevention: Make a restore point before Windows Update is allowed to replace audio drivers
Save a copy of the manufacturer's IDT audio installer for your laptop model
On older laptops, pause driver updates once you have a stable audio driver
Consider turning off Fast Startup if audio regularly breaks after shutting down and powering on

title: Intel Smart Sound Technology (Intel SST) OED: Code 10
codes: Intel Smart Sound Technology (Intel SST) OED
Intel Smart Sound Technology OED Code 10
summary: After a Windows update, the built-in speakers or microphone array stop behaving and Device Manager shows "This device cannot start. (Code 10)" on Intel Smart Sound Technology (Intel SST) OED. Microsoft has documented this driver incompatibility and responded with compatibility holds and updated drivers.
meaning: Intel SST is the audio DSP layer built into recent Intel platforms. It runs microphone arrays and low-power playback, and the OED (Offload Engine Driver) is one of the devices it exposes. If a Windows update lands on a system that does not have a compatible Intel SST driver, the OED device fails to start and reports Code 10. Microsoft confirmed this specific incompatibility, blocked affected PCs from receiving the problem update, and pushed corrected drivers through Windows Update and through PC manufacturers.
commonCauses: A Windows update was applied on top of an older Intel SST driver that is not compatible
A clean install left only generic audio drivers, with no OEM SST driver present
Windows Update's generic audio driver took the place of the manufacturer's SST stack
System firmware or BIOS is out of date on certain models

fixes.title: Look for the corrected driver in Windows Update
fixes.detail: Open Settings → Windows Update, choose Check for updates, and also review the optional driver updates. Microsoft distributed fixed Intel SST drivers this way. Install what is offered, restart, and check the device again in Device Manager.

fixes.title: Remove the device and scan for it again
fixes.detail: In `devmgmt.msc`, look under System devices (or Sound, video and game controllers), right-click 'Intel Smart Sound Technology (Intel SST) OED' and choose Uninstall device. Then run Action → Scan for hardware changes and restart the PC.

fixes.title: Install your manufacturer's Intel SST driver bundle
fixes.detail: From your laptop vendor's support page, download the Intel SST or audio driver bundle for your exact model and install it ahead of any generic replacement. These packages are sensitive to version, so both the model and the Windows version need to match.
fixes.riskNote: SST drivers break easily when versions do not line up. If your laptop maker offers its own bundle, use that rather than Intel's generic package.

fixes.title: Roll the driver back
fixes.detail: When Code 10 showed up straight after an update, open the device's Properties, select the Driver tab and click 'Roll Back Driver'. Then hold off on optional driver updates until a compatible SST release is available.

fixes.title: Bring the BIOS and firmware up to date
fixes.detail: Several laptop makers released firmware updates aimed specifically at SST stability. Install the newest BIOS from your manufacturer's support site with the charger connected, then test audio again.
fixes.riskNote: Do not interrupt a BIOS update under any circumstances, since that can leave the PC unable to start. Keep it plugged in until the update completes.

prevention: Install the manufacturer's audio and SST drivers before taking a major Windows upgrade
Set a restore point ahead of Windows feature updates
Keep the BIOS and firmware current on laptop models known to have SST problems

title: HDMI or DisplayPort monitor plays no sound
summary: Your external monitor shows a picture over HDMI or DisplayPort, yet no sound comes out of it. Either Windows is routing audio to another device, or the monitor's audio output is disabled, missing, or the connection cannot carry sound at all.
meaning: HDMI and DisplayPort transmit audio as well as video, and every GPU output provides its own audio endpoint (for example 'NVIDIA High Definition Audio' or 'Intel Display Audio') that appears only while a display is attached. The monitor stays silent, even with a working cable and picture, if Windows is still using an older device as the default, if the endpoint has been disabled, or if the graphics driver was installed without its HD Audio part.
commonCauses: Windows is still sending audio to the previous default device (speakers or headphones) rather than the monitor
The monitor's audio endpoint is disabled or not listed as a playback device
The graphics driver was installed without its HDMI/DisplayPort HD Audio component
The cable or adapter only passes video (such as passive HDMI to VGA or DVI adapters), or the monitor's own volume or input settings are off
Windows is holding on to an outdated endpoint after sleep, docking or switching monitors

fixes.title: Choose the monitor as your playback device
fixes.detail: Click the speaker icon on the taskbar, or open Settings → System → Sound, and select the monitor. It appears by name together with its GPU audio, for example 'DELL U2723QE (NVIDIA High Definition Audio)'. You can also use the classic dialog: press Win+R, run `mmsys.cpl`, open the Playback tab, select the monitor and click 'Set Default'.

fixes.title: Reveal and enable hidden playback devices
fixes.detail: Press Win+R, run `mmsys.cpl`, go to the Playback tab, right-click a blank area and choose 'Show Disabled Devices'. If the monitor shows up grayed out, right-click it, pick Enable, make it the default and test. Use this when the monitor has dropped off the output list completely.

fixes.title: Rule out the cable, adapter and monitor settings
fixes.detail: Open the monitor's on-screen menu and check its volume, mute setting and input source, then try another cable or port. Passive adapters to VGA or DVI cannot carry audio, and some TVs need audio output turned on in their own settings.

fixes.title: Reinstall the graphics driver with HD Audio included
fixes.detail: Install the complete driver package from NVIDIA, AMD or Intel. NVIDIA's custom install has a dedicated 'HD Audio driver' checkbox, while the full Intel and AMD packages bundle their display audio drivers. Restart when it finishes, since the monitor's audio endpoint only returns when that component is installed.
fixes.riskNote: The screen can flicker or go dark for a moment while the driver installs. That is expected, so let the installer finish.

fixes.title: Use the Playing Audio troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Open Settings → System → Troubleshoot → Other troubleshooters, find Playing Audio and click Run. It automatically checks the default device, disabled endpoints and the state of the audio services.

prevention: Check which output is the default each time you dock, reconnect or switch monitors
Install full graphics driver packages from the vendor rather than driver-only or generic versions
Pick adapters and docking stations that clearly list audio passthrough support

title: "The Windows Security Center Service can't be started"
codes: The Windows Security Center Service can't be started
Windows Security Center Service can't be started
security center service can't be started
summary: When you open Windows Security, a red banner warns that the Windows Security Center Service can't be started. The service that gathers protection status (wscsvc) is stopped, disabled, or failing to initialize.
meaning: Security Center pulls status information from Microsoft Defender Antivirus, the firewall and any third-party antivirus that has registered with Windows, then passes it to the Windows Security app. If the service is not running, the app displays the banner and the protection pages cannot report their state.
